articles.title: DJ Moore injury sparks surprise Bills suggestion as former NFL star names 9,811-yard WR as potential replacement
articles.summary: NFL News: The Buffalo Bills beat the Detroit Lions in their new stadium opener, but the win came with a cost. Wide receiver DJ Moore left the game in the second.
articles.body: The Buffalo Bills beat the Detroit Lions in their new stadium opener, but the win came with a cost. Wide receiver DJ Moore left the game in the second quarter with a shoulder stinger and never came back. Moore was ruled out for the remainder of the game, and with his status now uncertain heading into next week, the conversation has quickly shifted to who Buffalo might turn to if he misses time. Former NFL cornerback Darius Butler already has a name in mind, and it is one that Bills fans will recognize.Could Brandin Cooks be the answer if DJ Moore misses games?Butler posted on X that Brandin Cooks is going to be a Buffalo Bill by Sunday. He is speculating, but the suggestion is not without logic. Cooks visited the Baltimore Ravens on Thursday, which means he is clearly open to returning to the NFL. And the Bills, who know him well, could very much come calling.Cooks is 33 now and has not played this season, but the resume speaks for itself. Over 12 NFL seasons with the Saints, Patriots, Rams, Texans, Cowboys, and yes, the Bills, he has put up 9,811 receiving yards, 734 receptions, and 60 touchdowns across 173 games. Buffalo signed him last year, and though he only played five games, catching five passes for 114 yards, he still knows the offense and the culture around the building.The Bills did not trade a second-round pick to Chicago for Moore just to replace him with a stopgap. Moore was supposed to be Josh Allen's true No. 1 receiver, the kind Buffalo has not really had since Stefon Diggs was dealt to Houston before the 2024 season. So if Moore misses meaningful time, the pressure on everyone else goes up, not just on a potential free agent addition.How big is DJ Moore's absence for the Buffalo Bills offense?Moore's first two games as a Bill told you everything about why they wanted him. In Week 1 against the Texans, he caught five balls for 100 yards and a touchdown. Head coach Joe Brady was direct about what Moore brings. "Yeah, I mean, you see there's a reason we brought him here and the ability that he can make plays down the field. And look, we had a pass interference that's not even going to show up in the stat book, right? But that's another added bonus, right? You saw the different types of weapons that we had, with DJ having a big game, Dalton [Kincaid] had a big game," Brady said on Monday, via A to Z Sports.Kincaid has been genuinely good through two weeks. He caught five passes for 130 yards against Houston and followed that with seven catches for 95 yards and a score against Detroit. He can carry more load. But Moore's value goes beyond catch counts. His ability to draw pass interference, threaten deep, and move the chains on third down is not something you just replace with a name off the street.That is what makes the Cooks idea interesting rather than just a throwaway suggestion. He has been in those moments before. He understands what a No. 1 receiver is supposed to do in a system like this. Whether he can still do it at his age is the question Buffalo would need to answer quickly.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Sean McVay hopes Rams never play in Australia 'ever again'
articles.summary: McVay enjoyed the atmosphere Down Under, but is happy to return to a normal schedule of preparation.
articles.body:
It would make Sean McVay very happy if the Los Angeles Rams avoided playing in Australia again while he is head coach.

The Rams' much-talked-about trip Down Under ended in a 27-7 defeat to the San Francisco 49ers last week. It was a game to forget for McVay.

"I want to see us be present right now and move forward," McVay said Thursday . "That game is so far — it's almost like you try to do the 'Men in Black' thing where you say, 'Hey, I don't remember what happened. That was so long ago.' We're not playing in Australia ever again, I hope. Not because it wasn't a great atmosphere, that'll get taken out of context."

There were over 100,000 fans in attendance at the Melbourne Cricket Ground for the NFL's first-ever regular season game in Australia. It won't be the last time the league makes the trip as Brett Gosper, the NFL's head of Europe and Asia-Pacific, told the Australian Financial Review that there will be at least two more games over the next three seasons.

As McVay said, his sour experience had nothing to do with the country itself or everything outside of the game. As 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan this week said, it was tough to enjoy it all when you're focused on working.

The Rams head coach was back in his comfortable place this week: back home in Los Angeles as the team goes through a normal week of preparation as they host the New York Giants on Monday night .

"Bottom line is, I like the way that I feel of our preparation, eyes moving forward, chest out, chin up, eyes forward, and let's go be about it," McVay said. "Let's go prepare the right way. Let's have great focus and concentration. Let's have a great energy and an edge in which we prepare and compete with and then let's go be ready to go against a really damn good football team.

"What they looked like in Week 1, we got a great challenge ahead. That's what every week is. We're excited to compete. All we can do is really have a great day of preparation today."

articles.title: 3 things to know from Seattle Seahawks' Week 1 win
articles.summary: The Cardinals host the Seahawks in Week 2. What can we learn from Seattle's season-opening win?
articles.body:
The Arizona Cardinals will be at home in Week 2 facing the defending champion Seattle Seahawks . The Cardinals are coming off a Week 1 26-14 upset win over the Los Angeles Chargers . The Seahawks rallied from down 10-0 to beat the New England Patriots 13-10 behind backup quarterback Drew Lock , who entered the game after Sam Darnold exited in the first quarter with a gluteal injury.

What can the Cardinals expect from the Seahawks in Week 2? There are three things to know from the Seahawks' Week 1 win.

They picked off Patriots quarterback Drake Maye three times in Week 1, all three times in the fourth quarter. And the Seahawks capitalized, scoring after the first two takeaways to take the lead and then running the clock out after the final interception in the end zone.

They do not allow running backs to get yards

The Patriots rushed for 109 yards, but 47 of those came from Maye scrambling. Seattle's defense held Rhamondre Stevenson and former Cardinal Corey Kiner to 62 yards on 24 attempts, an average of 2.6 yards per carry.

Receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba was last season's Offensive Player of the Year, and he started the season dominant. He had eight receptions for 122 yards and a touchdown in Week 1. He is their top target. The Seahawks attempted 24 passes in Week 1. Eleven were thrown JSN's way.

articles.title: Updated NFL MVP odds after Josh Allen’s epic 5 touchdown performance
articles.summary: Josh Allen accounted for five touchdowns against the Detroit Lions on Thursday night.
articles.body:
Josh Allen is the favorite to win NFL MVP. It still very early in the season, but he's on pace for the type of historic season that we've only really seen from Patrick Mahomes and Peyton Manning during seasons they won the award and took their teams deep into the postseason.

Allen was the favorite after Week 1 and a dominant performance against the Detroit Lions in the Bills' first game at Highmark Stadium only increased his lead over Lamar Jackson . After his five touchdown game on Thursday Night Football Allen moved from +475 to +260.

While Allen's big night didn't affect Lamar Jackson's odds much, if at all, it did make Caleb Williams drop from +750 to +1100.

articles.title: Titans 'Fully Committed' to Cam Ward Despite 'Rough' Week 1 vs. Jets, Robert Saleh Says
articles.summary: Tennessee Titans coach Robert Saleh expressed faith in quarterback Cam Ward's ability to bounce back from his accuracy issues in a Week 1 loss to the New York Jets.
articles.body:
Tennessee Titans coach Robert Saleh expressed faith in quarterback Cam Ward's ability to bounce back from his accuracy issues in a Week 1 loss to the New York Jets.

"We're fully committed to Cam because we believe in him," Saleh told ESPN's Turron Davenport . "You've got to let these young men grow.

"You would hate to be on the other side of it where you give up on a young man, and he goes to another team, and he wins a Super Bowl. We believe he has the right mindset, and we're going to give him every opportunity to grow."

Saleh previously admitted Ward had a "rough" outing in last Sunday's 23-10 season-opening loss to the Titans. Ward struggled under pressure while completing 19 of 32 pass attempts for 140 yards, and his one passing touchdown came late in the fourth quarter.

The Titans coach also said Ward has been "very receptive" about making adjustments to his game heading into Week 2.

"He's going to get better," Saleh told reporters earlier this week, before adding Ward could be helped by teammates and coaches also improving their game.

"To say he's going in the wrong direction, I don't think that'd be fair," Saleh said. "He's a young kid."

Ward and the Titans are preparing this week to face the Philadelphia Eagles, who are coming off a Week 1 victory in which they held Washington Commanders quarter Jayden Daniels to 164 passing yards.

Saleh will hope whatever mid-week adjustments his coaching staff is working on with Ward can make a difference as the second-year quarterback gears up to take on the Eagles defense this Sunday at 1 p.m. ET. in Nashville.

articles.title: Buffalo Bills fans pay eye-opening prices for beer and food at Highmark Stadium opener
articles.summary: Pinto Ron's bowling ball shots, beer horns and hour-long concession lines define the wild Bills Mafia tailgate scene in Orchard Park, New York.
articles.body: The sun is shining this morning in Buffalo, New York as I pump out an edition of Friday Screencaps before hopping in the car for the drive back around Lake Erie to a whole different world from what I just experienced in Orchard Park. My mission going in from my boss was simple: Go ask questions, talk to the people and document the opening of the new Highmark Stadium. What I experienced was what I suspect it's like to be on a drug-induced trip like those people in San Francisco experience where they're taking dumps in the streets and hunched over in paralysis as the drugs run wild through the bloodstream. Gameday in Buffalo is unlike anything I've ever experienced, and I've been to all the biggest mainstream sports experiences in the U.S. NEWLY RELEASED DATA SHOWS WHICH AMERICAN CITIES HAVE THE MOST PASSIONATE FANBASES IN THE NFL The locals don't even blink at the sight of guys like this who are about to delete 32 beers. The real members of Bills Mafia have their own looks. Thousands of looks. They don't even blink at a 400-pounder walking around with his rack hanging out. This is a place where adults make the pilgrimage to the legendary Pinto Ron and Pizza Pete tailgate spot in the Hammer Lot where Pinto Ron's team of merry pranksters pour shots of liquor into a bowling ball finger hole. Drinking the shot is just one part of the routine. Throwing the ball to the ground and then blowing on a vuvuzela is also included in the bit. For the ladies, Ron's crew provides cherries that are dangled over their faces. Most of the classy women will not suck the cherry off the stem. Some, however, go for the full experience. I assume the cherries have been soaked in moonshine. BUFFALO BILLS' LATEST EDITION TO THEIR NEW STADIUM IS PREDICTABLY (AND PAINFULLY) ON BRAND Hundreds and hundreds of people drink the shot out of the same hole over the course of a tailgate. Sanitation isn't a thing here. The liquor kills the germs. Pinto Ron's team also cooks right on the hood of the most famous Pinto in Buffalo. Bacon and dogs were on the menu Thursday. Yes, I'm told the Pinto runs. LIONS AVOID FRANCHISE-WORST COLLAPSE AS DEFENSE STOPS SAINTS TWO-POINT CONVERSION IN OT Meanwhile, about 20 yards from Ron's holy grail of tailgating, Lions fans had their own headquarters. That's where the infamous Tubgaters held court with their traveling hot tub that is mounted on a trailer. The owner tells me that when he rolls into town, he'll pull up to a house and ask the locals if he can fill up his tub. On Thursday, he had the water up to 98 degrees, but he assured me it could get up to 115 degrees for those really cold winter nights. Buffalo Bills games are Disney World for NFL tailgating debauchery, but there's a method to the madness. People are cordial. Free food is very common. It's everywhere. Free liquor is everywhere. Friendship isn't hard to come by. You can arrive by yourself and leave with dozens of friends. RYAN FITZPATRICK SAYS FRIENDS RAVING ABOUT HIGHMARK STADIUM DESPITE HARSH CRITICS: 'ABSOLUTELY UNBELIEVABLE' Needless to say, I'll be back. My dad needs to see this. 📩 Email: joe.kinsey@outkick.comSend photos, stories, tips, rants—whatever you've got. 📰 Screencaps Page:👉 Read the latest Screencaps ▶️ YouTube: Screencaps with Joe KinseySubscribe for videos, rants, and behind-the-scenes. 🐦 Twitter/X: @JoeKinseyexpTag me or drop a DM. 📸 Instagram: @OutKickScreencapsYou guys need to start tagging me on content you're seeing. 📘 Facebook Page: Screencaps on Facebook 👥 Facebook Group: Join the Screencaps Community 📬 Mail (Thursday Night Mowing League):27072 Carronade Dr, Unit A 155Perrysburg, OH 43551 Highmark Stadium review: It's LOUD & a beer with a beer horn will run you $30 When I think of loud stadiums, I think of places like Autzen Field in Oregon or Arrowhead. Highmark Stadium IS LOUD. It's loud from the second you walk in. The music being played pregame was LOUD, super loud. The in-game experience is the same thing. I'm talking piercing noise. The other big takeaway for fans has to be concession pricing. Not that we should be shocked. I found this couple who just exited a concession room where they picked up the prized Bills beer horns and some food. Here's what you get for $113: • Two beers (16 oz, I believe) • Two of the prized beer horns – yes, they have lids so you don't spill beer as you're walking around • A bucket of popcorn • A personal pizza Other food prices that I spotted: • Souvenir bucket of popcorn: $19 • Dill pickle popcorn: $10 • Pierogies: $14 • Sweet Italian sausage on a sub roll: $14 CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE • Order of chicken wings (I assume you get six): $18 Other observations from Highmark: – The concourses are a mess in the areas where they're selling the beer horns. In one area of the 300 level, an escalator dumps fans into an area where fans had waited over an hour for the horns. "How long have you been waiting for a beer," I asked one guy. "An hour and fifteen minutes," the guy replied. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! I thought he was screwing with me. "Are you serious," I fired back. That's when others in line spoke up. He wasn't lying. An hour or more wait was common. But, if you were to ask a Bills fan if the lines, and prices, and insanely packed concourses were worth it after the Bills worked over the Lions in their new stadium, they'd tell you it was all worth it to watch Josh Allen have another career night. All was right in the world as long as you don't look at your credit card statement. ################ SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER And with that, I'm going to close down my Buffalo operation and get home to Ohio. articles.title: Josh Allen Makes NFL History with Rare Stats After Wins vs. Texans, Lions to Open Season
articles.summary: Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen started the 2026 season with one of the most productive two-game stretches in NFL history.
articles.body:
Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen started the 2026 season with one of the most productive two-game stretches in NFL history.

Allen recorded his ninth touchdown of the season as the Bills orchestrated a 41-31 win over the Detroit Lions.

Allen joined former Hall of Famer Ernie Nevers as the second player in NFL history to rack up nine total touchdowns and at least four rushing touchdowns in a five-day span, according to Opta Stats (h/t Bills PR).

The feat was last achieved by Nevers with the Arizona Cardinals in 1929.

Allen passed for two touchdowns and ran in two more last Sunday during the Bills' season-opening win at the Houston Texans.

He recorded another five touchdowns, including three passing and two rushing, during Thursday's victory over the visiting Lions.

Allen has completed 66.7 percent of his passes and thrown no interceptions during the Bills' 2-0 start to the season. He'll now get a longer break before the Bills return to action a week from Sunday with a home game against the Los Angeles Chargers.

articles.title: Josh Allen on an MVP mission as his 5 TDs help Bills destroy Lions 41-31 in first game at new Highmark Stadium
articles.summary: Josh Allen had his second straight huge game to start the season.
articles.body: Matthew Stafford won NFL MVP last season, but few questioned Josh Allen's standing as the top quarterback in the league. Allen had settled into an elite level that few players have reached. And then, to start the 2026 season, Allen had a surprise for everyone. He apparently was capable of leveling up. Allen is playing the best football of his career, and that's saying something. The Buffalo Bills quarterback has one MVP award already and a second one seems inevitable given the first couple games of the season, Allen was a force in a 41-31 victory over the Detroit Lions, which was the first regular-season game in $2.2 billion Highmark Stadium. Allen had 248 passing yards, 69 rushing yards, 3 passing touchdowns and 2 rushing touchdowns. He has 10 games with two passing touchdowns and two rushing touchdowns in a game. Nobody else in NFL history has more than four, via Josh Dubow of the Associated Press. Thursday night's game followed up another phenomenal performance, as Allen torched a very good Houston Texans defense in Week 1 including a game-winning touchdown in the final minutes of a 36-31 win. The Bills got off to a scorching start. Allen had 154 passing yards and three touchdowns, with 40 rushing yards and a touchdown, and there was still 2:52 left in the second quarter. The Lions' defense is decimated due to injuries in the secondary, but it's still not easy to put up those numbers in a half. The Bills had 299 yards and 20 first downs at halftime, and were averaging 8.3 yards per play. The Lions made it a game by getting a field goal at the end of the first half and a touchdown to begin the second half. They trailed 27-17 at that point. Allen answered with a long drive, capping it with his second rushing touchdown of the night. Detroit looked helpless.It's going to be difficult for Allen to keep up this pace or anything close because that would be unprecedented in NFL history. But it's also possible we're in the early stages of witnessing a truly historic season. Josh Allen is off to a scorching start this NFL season.AP Photo/Jeffrey T. BarnesJosh Allen has another huge nightThe Bills had the motivation of a hyped-up crowd for the first game in a new $2.2 billion Highmark Stadium. The start they had was stunning. The Bills drove downfield easily to start the game, and it ended with Allen scoring the first touchdown in the stadium's history on a 1-yard sneak. The second drive ended with Joshua Palmer running wide open downfield, no Lion within 10 yards of him, and Allen finding him for a 43-yard touchdown. The Bills were ready to put on a show during a historic night. The Lions' injured secondary was no match for the NFL's best quarterback.Allen got touchdown passes on each of the Bills' next two drives as well. He threw one to Dawson Knox and another to Dalton Kincaid. Allen's skills haven't been seen often in NFL history. He's a powerful runner who is already tied for 18th all time in career rushing touchdowns because he's hard to stop near the goal line. He has rare arm talent, and worked to become one of the NFL's more accurate quarterbacks. He can throw from the pocket or use his escapability to get away from the rush and find someone downfield. He's as well-rounded as any quarterback we've seen, and all of his skills seem to be peaking this season. Lions struggle to slow down BillsThe Lions were on the wrong side of a memorable night in Buffalo. Detroit's defense started the season well but has fallen apart since early in the third quarter of Week 1. The Saints' final six drives last week resulted in four touchdowns, a field goal and a missed field goal. The Bills' first four drives Thursday resulted in touchdowns. Finally, with 44 seconds left in the half against the Bills, the Lions got a stop on third down and forced a punt. When the Bills didn't get a huge gain on a play or have the Lions commit a penalty, it was a surprise. Buffalo was doing whatever it wanted. The Lions offered very little resistance. The Lions have significant questions about their defense. But the Texans looked bad on defense last week too. Many Bills opponents will. Joe Brady took over at head coach after serving as offensive coordinator last season, and he seems more willing to open up the offense than Sean McDermott was. That helps Allen, as does the health of Kincaid and DJ Moore, who unfortunately left Thursday's game with a shoulder injury. It's a great setup for Allen to have a career year, when he was already on a Hall of Fame path. Allen will have a good shot to win his second MVP award, but that's not what Allen or the Bills are chasing. They want a Super Bowl. With Allen looking like he is hitting a new peak, there might not be anything holding Buffalo back from it this season.

articles.title: Derrick Henry Praised by Barry Sanders, LaDainian Tomlinson After Making NFL History in Week 1
articles.summary: Baltimore Ravens running back Derrick Henry is earning admiration from some of the NFL's all-time greats amid his dominant performance in Sunday's season-opening win over the Indianapolis Colts.
articles.body:
Baltimore Ravens running back Derrick Henry is earning admiration from some of the NFL's all-time greats amid his dominant performance in Sunday's season-opening win over the Indianapolis Colts.

Both LaDainian Tomlinson and Barry Sanders praised Henry when speaking with The Athletic's Jeff Zrebiec .

"To me, he's the modern-day Jim Brown. That's what he is," Tomlinson told Zrebiec.

Sanders also compared Henry to Brown as well as Earl Campbell, according to Zrebiec.

"I just admire his consistent greatness... From high school to the Heisman and soon to the Hall, he has been great at every level, and it's hard to be consistent at such a high level over so many years," Sanders said, per Zrebiec.

Sanders added: "What Derrick has done from a young age until now is just incredible. I love to watch him run."

Henry ran for 144 yards with three touchdowns in Sunday's Week 1 matchup against the Colts to move past Marcus Allen for third on the NFL's all-time rushing touchdown leaderboard.

He now trails only Emmitt Smith and Tomlinson, who scored 164 and 145 career rushing touchdowns, respectively.

Smith said earlier this week he felt Henry would eventually be able to break his all-time rushing touchdown record.

That's not the only leaderboard Henry might be climbing this season. He's also heading into Week 2 just 97 yards behind Eric Dickerson for ninth on the NFL's all-time rushing leaderboard.

After racking up 1,595 rushing yards last year, Henry doesn't look like he's slowed down one game into his age-32 season.

He'll next look to challenge a New Orleans Saints run defense that allowed the Detroit Lions' Jahmyr Gibbs to rack up 156 rushing yards when the Ravens kick off their home opener Sunday at 1 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Week 2 Fantasy Football Rankings, Box Score Projections for Players with Top Matchups
articles.summary: Week 2 got underway with Thursday night's battle between the Detroit Lions and Buffalo Bills. Heading into the bulk of the schedule, some managers may already be scrambling to cover ground.
articles.body:
Week 2 got underway with Thursday night's battle between the Detroit Lions and Buffalo Bills. Heading into the bulk of the schedule, some managers may already be scrambling to cover ground.

Fortunately, some matchups are primed to provide catch-up opportunities. We'll review Week 1 results and project player roles to identify them.

Here, you'll find updated point-per-reception (PPR) rankings for each key position, along with projections for the matchups we love the most.

Matchup to Love: Baker Mayfield vs. Cleveland Browns

Baker Mayfield had a fumbling problem against the Cincinnati Bengals in Week 1 that severely limited his fantasy production. Assuming he exercises better ball security in Week 2, he should be one of the top fantasy plays of the week.

Mayfield and the Bucs will be eager to put their Week 1 loss behind them, and the visiting Cleveland Browns are the QB's former team. Mayfield often finds reasons to play with a chip on his shoulder, but in this case, he's truly getting a revenge-game opportunity.

Back in 2022, the Browns jettisoned Mayfield in order to make their ill-fated trade for Deshaun Watson. Expect Mayfield to remind Cleveland what it gave up on early and often in this matchup.

And the Browns are unlikely to do much to limit him. They surrendered the fifth-most fantasy points to opposing QBs in Week 1.

Box Score Projection: 336 passing yards, 3 TDs, 42 rushing yards

Christian McCaffrey, San Francisco 49ers

Matchup to Love: Kenneth Walker III vs. Indianapolis Colts

Even with a healthy Patrick Mahomes in the lineup, the Kansas City Chiefs leaned heavily on new running back Kenneth Walker III in Week 1. The former Seattle Seahawks standout went off against the Denver Broncos, recording one of the top fantasy performances at any position in the opening slate.

Walker racked up 173 rushing yards, three receptions, 18 receiving yards, and two touchdowns.

While Walker may not be as productive in Week 2, he's a high-floor play against an Indianapolis Colts defense that often looked lost in Week 1. Facing bruising back Derrick Henry certainly had something to do with it, but the Colts surrendered the third-most fantasy points to opposing RBs.

Expect Kansas City to lean on Walker once again in its second prime-time matchup of the season.

Box Score Projection: 124 rushing yards, 3 receptions, 22 receiving yards, 1 TD

Matchup to Love: Justin Jefferson at Chicago Bears

It appears that the Minnesota Vikings will roll with quarterback Carson Wentz in Week 2. He played most of Week 1 after starter Kyler Murray exited with a concussion, and while he didn't produce an eye-popping stat line, he did show strong chemistry with star receiver Justin Jefferson.

Jefferson finished Week 1 with eight catches, 92 yards, and two touchdowns.

The Chicago Bears, meanwhile, won a Week 1 shootout in which defense appeared optional. The Bears did force enough turnovers to eventually pull away for a 59-37 victory. However, they also surrendered the sixth-most fantasy points to opposing WRs.

This should be another back-and-forth offensive game. Expect Jefferson to play a massive role in it.

Box Score Projection: 9 receptions, 118 yards, 2 TDs

Matchup to Love: Harold Fannin Jr. at Tampa Bay Buccaneers

The Browns are likely to spend the entirety of Week 2 playing from behind. Unfortunately, their crop of wide receivers is likely to struggle against a Bucs' defense that held Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins in check last week.

Chase and Higgins combined for just five catches and 71 yards.

The Bengals, though, poked holes in Tampa's defense with tight end Mike Gesicki, who finished with five catches for 78 yards and a touchdown. Expect Cleveland to try a similar approach by targeting Harold Fannin Jr. early and often.

Don't expect Fannin to be quite as productive as Gesicki because Deshaun Watson isn't nearly as efficient as Joe Burrow. However, a high target share should give him a strong PPR floor.

Box Score Projection: 6 receptions, 76 yards

articles.title: Rob Gronkowski Reveals Patriots Gave No. 87 Jersey to Romeo Doubs Without Consulting Him
articles.summary: The New England Patriots apparently didn't check with Rob Gronkowski before giving the No. 87 jersey to wide receiver Romeo Doubs.
articles.body:
The New England Patriots apparently didn't check with Rob Gronkowski before giving the No. 87 jersey to wide receiver Romeo Doubs.

When asked this week on Up & Adams about Doubs' number selection, Gronkowski told Kay Adams, "I'm not the one who makes the decisions over there."

"I wasn't consulted at all, but I mean, I'm cool with it," Gronkowski told Adams. "The only number that I truly believe that should be retired in New England... is the No. 12."

Gronkowski continued, "If you're not playing for 20 years, I don't think that any other number should be retired. I think all other numbers should be very usable."

The Patriots retired Tom Brady's No. 12 ahead of the 2024 season. The franchise had previously retired seven other jerseys, but none since Bruce Armstrong in 2001.

New England signed Doubs to a four-year, $70 million contract as a top option for Drake Maye alongside A.J. Brown this offseason.

Doubs, who wore No. 87 for four seasons with the Green Bay Packers, claimed the jersey again after arriving in New England.

Gronkowski donned the same number throughout his nine seasons with the Patriots, during which he contributed to three Super Bowl runs alongside Brady.

The tight end is set to be inducted into the Patriots Hall of Fame this November and is a candidate to join the Pro Football Hall of Fame as a member of the Class of 2027.

Doubs struggled last week in the Patriots' season-opening loss to the Seattle Seahawks, during which he recorded no catches and dropped a pass in his team's 13-10 loss.

Now that Brown is sidelined for an anticipated six weeks with a high ankle sprain, the Patriots will hope more than ever Doubs can live up to the legacy of his jersey number as his team prepares for Sunday's home opener against the Pittsburgh Steelers.

articles.title: Ranking the Top 20 New York Rangers Prospects Ahead of the 2026-27 Season
articles.summary: General Manager Chris Drury may insist that the Rangers aren't in a rebuild, and the team's splashy offseason reinforces that they are gunning for contention as soon as possible.
articles.body:
General Manager Chris Drury may insist that the Rangers aren't in a rebuild, and the team's splashy offseason reinforces that they are gunning for contention as soon as possible.

That does not mean the prospect pool is an afterthought. In fact, the state of the youth will be integral to righting the ship in New York. To some extent, that is about injecting impact players into the lineup. They surely hope they found a solution in fifth-overall pick Alberts Šmits. Drury also targeted pro-ready players in trades, including Cole Beaudoin and Liam Greentree.

It's also about giving yourself ammunition in the trade market. A successful prospect pool will not be able to fit all players into the NHL lineup. Some inevitably will have to become trade bait. Among the reasons the Rangers have failed to add impact NHLers is that they have lacked the talent other teams are seeking.

The Rangers still have a lot of work to do, and the prospect pool grades out as average by NHL standards. That is, however, a meaningful improvement from where the depth chart sat in previous seasons. In particular, the team's prospect depth is great. I see at least 20 prospects with a reasonable chance of becoming NHLers.

Let's take a look at the Rangers' top-20 NHL prospects.

In my view, Gonchar deserves more attention than he has received.

One reason he's an interesting prospect is that he is an unorthodox player who doesn't fit the low-hanging fruit the Rangers have been drafting for in recent years.

The nephew of former NHL superstar Sergei, Gonchar is a pure offensive defenseman. He isn't a great skater but still finds ways to pivot out of pressure along the blue line. He relies heavily on misdirection to create space to attack. He loves to move lower in the zone and is a smooth puck-mover, even when his body is contorted in various ways. His shot itself is lethal — hard and often shelf — but he also freezes defenses and goaltenders with fakes. The "will he, won't he" of it all makes other teams nervous.

Fifteen goals in the OHL last season are encouraging, and although 51 total points in 65 games is less than stellar, the Sudbury Wolves were a very low-scoring team overall; not a single forward was above a point per game.

Offense aside, it's pretty ugly. He's below-average speed-wise; he's well under the weight he'll need to play at in professional hockey, and his physical game is non-existent. He turns 20 in late October, so he doesn't have much developmental runway left. Still, his offensive toolbox is sophisticated and not worth giving up on yet.

The Rangers acquired Battaglia as a face-saving measure for their Brennan Othmann failure. At the time of acquisition, he was a credible NHL prospect but with a lot of warts. To his credit, Battaglia's play improved post-acquisition, and he really turned on the jets in the OHL playoffs: five goals and 13 assists in eight games.

Battaglia, a former second-round pick, is a strong winger who often gets his way in board battles and can brute-force his way to the net. He also has professional-caliber hands and a keen hockey sense. He is somewhat dynamic carrying the puck through the neutral zone and can make some nice passing combinations with teammates when holding the puck low in the zone.

Strength, hands, and hockey sense are strong building blocks for an NHL bottom-six winger.

The Achilles' heel is his skating. There's no way around it. He skates like there is lead in his boots. The straight-line speed is okay, but he is slow at the jump. The Rangers' skills team will have to help him gain a lot more power in his stride. Otherwise, he'll be destined for a career in the AHL.

If one were to design the type of player the Rangers want to target in the mid-to-late rounds of the NHL Draft, Charlie Morrison would come close.

The QMJHL defenseman is 6'3" and a well-above-average skater. His straight-line speed is strong, and his four-way mobility is polished for his age and projection. That ability to move sets the stage for his aggressive playing style. He loves to line up puck carriers and then pounce with a crushing hit. He jumps into gaps to disrupt a rush or pick off a lateral pass. Morrison is hungry to disrupt, and he has the physical tools to make it happen. Stylistically, he fits where the Rangers are trying to go with their defensemen.

His game is a double-edged sword at the moment. When his aggressive decisions work, it's great. Too often, the untamed style can backfire. This is not unusual for an 18-year-old and the Rangers will happily take their chance on an ambitious player. It beats the alternative of someone afraid to make mistakes. It will be on the development staff to help him pick his moments better.

Morrison is sloppy at handling the puck. This will never be his strength, though he will need to make gains to meet the minimum standard for an NHL defenseman. The tools were enough to justify his third-round slotting this past June and he projects as a physical shutdown third-pairing defenseman in the NHL.

When the Rangers drafted Lamb in 2021, he was a raw high school talent who everyone knew would need to take the scenic route to the NHL. He signed with the Rangers in the Spring after a four-year career at the University of Minnesota. Lamb appeared to be cooking his sophomore season, posting 27 points in 39 games while playing third-line minutes. He seemed poised for a big upperclassman bump. It never came. He totaled 26 points in 39 games as a junior and 30 in 35 as a senior while leading all Gophers forwards in ice time (per InStat).

To be fair, the Gophers were undergoing a transition period and were a very low-scoring team. I thought it was a 50/50 shot that the Rangers would give Lamb an entry-level contract. He did and joined the Hartford Wolf Pack, where he removed any doubt about that decision: he played well, scoring four goals and adding five assists in 15 games for a struggling Wolf Pack team.

Lamb has matured a lot as a player. He is an astute forechecker who cuts off passing lanes in the layered way the Rangers' systems call for. He has good habits on the ice and heightened instincts with the puck on his stick. He's going to be a good pro for the Wolf Pack, and that shouldn't be taken for granted. The AHL team has been in disarray, and part of righting the ship is having young contributors who don't count towards the veteran max.

Beyond that, I am skeptical. He lacks any standout traits, whether physical (skating, size) or in terms of vision and puck skills. If he adds more dynamic qualities, I can see him turning into a Jonny Brodzinski-type as a utility 13th forward.

Barnhill is one of many in the Rangers' system who fit a theme: He's big, he's fast, and he's a shutdown defenseman.

The 6'6" took a big leap to NCAA hockey last season, playing third-pairing minutes for a contender in Michigan State. The box scores won't impress anyone: No goals, six assists, and four assists in 37 games. That's not a good way to assess Barnhill.

The Arizona native is 6'6" and a powerful skater. That's already a good starting point for any defense prospect. Despite how raw he is overall, it's no surprise he held his own in the NCAA because he is physically built for it. He is powerful in board battles. He can cover a lot of ice but also has good footwork so as to not get beat in small-ice defensive moments. He's physical around the front of the net but also defends with aplomb, holding measured gaps and angling puck carriers to the perimeter.

There is little offense to his game (as the numbers reflect), but he is competent at retrieving pucks and finding simple passes from the defensive zone. He held his own in third-pairing minutes, averaging a little over 14 minutes per game. Michigan State's top-three defensemen from last season have moved on to pro hockey, and Barnhill should see a massive bump in ice time as a sophomore. He's a breakout candidate for 2026-27.

In 2025-2026, Nathan Aspinall went from an interesting late-round pick to a bona fide NHL prospect. He more than doubled his previous OHL production, scoring 33 goals and adding 61 assists in 65 games. Then he absolutely dominated in the playoffs, scoring 10 goals and adding 7 assists in 8 games.

The impetus for the Rangers originally drafting him in round five is his 6'7" frame. He doesn't play an overly vicious game, but he does lean into his size. He uses his reach to protect pucks and disrupt defenders holding the puck at the point. He is very hard to move.

The pleasant surprise has been his offensive acumen. When the Rangers drafted him, he had already shown solid hands around the net. He's really expanded that part of his game and you see him combining traits to into effective sequences. For instance, he'll use his size to create separation from a defender while holding the puck up upon a zone entry, then make a deft pass to the weak side as a defenseman slides low. He has no problems stickhandling close to his body. And he has an absolute rocket of a shot.

The trick will be transitioning him to play a different style of game in professional hockey. He's not going to play power-play minutes in the NHL. He has defensive awareness, and now the coaching staff in Hartford needs to help him hone in on a role as a checking forward. The tools are there, and he has a very real chance of becoming a unique fourth-line winger.

After a surprising first pro season in which he led the 2024-25 Hartford Wolf Pack in goals (20), Roobroeck's sophomore season was more muted, scoring 11 goals and 15 assists in 72 games.

It's not what you want to see, but there are mitigating circumstances. Overall, the Wolf Pack were an extremely low-scoring team. More specifically, Roobroeck's most common linemate, Anton Blidh, was a black hole offensively.

Roobroeck is a toolsy 6'7" center who is stylistically a perfect match for his theoretical fourth-line upside. He doesn't cheat the game. He drops deep in the defensive zone to offer outlets on breakouts or to help create numbers advantages in puck scrums. He sticks tight to his checks. He's always supporting the defensive zone of the puck during neutral zone scrums. He uses his reach effectively in the defensive zone to cut off shooting lanes or pressure the puck at the point without overpursuing.

Offensively, Roobroeck has some calm in his game even if he lacks soft skills. His wrist shot is great, and he'll roof pucks past goaltenders from distance. You'd like to see him become meaner around the net, and he needs to add some more explosion to his first step. Roobroeck will also need to improve his faceoff skills on the left side of the ice to carve that out as a specialty.

The baseline pro abilities are all there. Now it's about fine-tuning. If he can reduce some of those deficits, then he has a chance to establish a long NHL career as a fourth-line center. Look for him to get his first NHL opportunity next season.

The New York native was a steady presence in his three years patrolling the Boston College blue line. I thought he played some of his best hockey for gold medal-winning Team USA at the 2025 World Junior Championships. For his junior 2025-2026 season, I got to see him in action a number of times (including once in person), and his development was once again notable but measured: some added strength and more command of the puck in the offensive zone.

Fortescue knows his strengths, and he sticks to them. He gaps up nicely against the rush and drives puck carriers wide with his stick as an anchor. He does a solid job retrieving dump-ins and finding short, simple outlets. He has average four-way mobility, and I like that he's added some oomph to his protecting the top of the crease when pucks are high in the zone.

He held his own in nine NHL games last season, but it would have been scrutinized more if the games mattered. He will probably start the 2026-2027 season in the AHL. All-in-all, I think Fortescue a perfectly fine prospect but I don't see any standout traits that are commensurate with the particularly high value the Rangers (and some other NHL teams) place on him as a prospect. The baseline is good enough for his path to a career as a third-pairing shutdown defenseman to be evident, though I don't think it's guaranteed.

Vladislav Gavrikov and Marcus Pettersson are locked in on the left side, and Matthew Robertson has better physical attributes and is already more proven. Of course, room will have to be made for Alberts Šmits soon enough, as is. I have to wonder if his eventual utility to the Rangers is as a critical trade chip to add an impact forward within the next two seasons.

I maintain that Scott Morrow was a reasonable addition to the K'Andre Miller trade. Sometimes things just don't work out.

He was bad for the Rangers in 2025-26. The lineup was screaming for an offensive defenseman to make an impact, especially when Adam Fox was injured. Six assists in 29 games won't cut it. While some of his puck movement from the defensive end was helpful, he also struggled with the speed of the pressure and gave up some rough turnovers.

Defensively, it was ugly. Even in sheltered minutes, he got piled on.

The real shocker to me, however, was how pedestrian he looked in the AHL. His 19 points in 39 games were a step back, and he did not control the pace like he had the previous season as an AHL All-Star.

There are mitigating circumstances, sure. It was a tough environment for a young player to jump into. The Rangers, on the whole, clearly need to rethink their organizational philosophies and procedures. At this point, it probably doesn't matter.

This is the second NHL team with whom he has struggled to establish himself. He's boxed out of a regular lineup spot, and the addition of Sean Durzi to the right side makes even the idea of Morrow as a sheltered offensive defenseman redundant.

If he is a Ranger next season, it will be because he radically redefined his game and proved it well enough in training camp to earn a spot as a seventh or eighth defenseman. If he doesn't make the opening-night lineup, he'll have to go through waivers. His Rangers' career is on life support.

For me, Eriksen is the most underappreciated prospect in the Rangers' pool.

The Norwegian center blends a high hockey IQ with increasingly developed physical tools. He is deceptive with the puck. He scans his options before skating onto pucks and plans proactively rather than reacting. He is a big driver of offense because he is unpredictable while in motion.

His teammates at the junior level would send him the puck as the default, almost like a point guard in basketball. The production proves why: 19 goals and 25 assists in 25 J20 games is comical. He got a sniff of pro hockey in the Allsvenskan (Swedish second tier) last season and played respectable defensive hockey while showing sporadic flashes of offense.

In the lead-up to the 2026-2027 Swedish Hockey League campaign, Eriksen has gotten some more reps in the J20 league. He appears to have grown physically. His skating is now more explosive, and his shot is harder. Add that to his already existing agility and ability to dissect within the offensive zone, and the Rangers have a legitimate center prospect marinating.

He's ready for the SHL, and it shouldn't be forgotten that he only just turned 19 on Sept. 13. I think Eriksen is a bona fide B-tier prospect with a legitimate chance to become a middle-six center. While all teams believe in their prospects, I was told the Rangers were particularly thrilled that Eriksen was available in round four in 2025 and, a season later, he's outpacing that slotting.

Chmelař is an interesting prospect because his statistical profile does not suggest he is worth pondering. A sophomore NCAA season with 15 points in 26 games. Eight goals and 25 total points in 46 AHL games last season. That is not what an NHLer typically looks like.

The tape doesn't lie, though. His NHL call-up may have been opportunistic, but he took advantage of that chance. Four goals in 28 games while averaging only 9:09 of ice time. The Rangers controlled possession during his shifts (a 53.7 expected goals percentage). It was a strong cameo appearance, even if the games weren't meaningful for the standings.

Chmelař is 6'4,", and his strength is hard to miss. He's a bulldozer below the faceoff dots. He protects the puck, creates a lot of traffic in front of the net, and deposits junk from rebounds and broken plays into the net.

The biggest difference for Chmelař at age 21, compared to his teens, is he is now a really powerful skater. His straight-line burst ranked among the best in the NHL last season, and we saw his success in scoring from transition plays in the neutral zone.

His game has limits, but he plays within the bounds of his strengths. He should be in the opening-night lineup unless he really struggles in training camp, and I think he's headed toward a full-time job on the Rangers' fourth line for the next few seasons.

Sŷkora's production in the AHL the past three seasons would be all but disqualifying for a 5'10" winger. Last season was his "best" at 12 goals and 17 assists in 62 games, or under .5 points per game. While I will admit to growing increasingly skeptical of his NHL prospects in light of plateauing production at 21 years old, the "under the hood" math offered some hope; Sŷkora has consistently been one of Hartford's best at tilting the ice away from the defensive side and towards offensive possessions.

It's funny that his offensive explosion actually came during his first NHL stint. Three goals and an assist in nine games while playing bottom-six minutes. Rangers fans will remember that his offense mostly comes from an infinite turbo button. He's fast, he's a hard worker, and he's aggressive pursuing pucks. Add in that he is vocal and passionate, and you have the makings of a true heart-and-soul player injected into a team that needs it.

A stint in end-of-season action is one thing. Can Sŷkora sustain it over a full season when there is more pressure and the coaching staff is honed in on tactical minutiae? The speed and energy are great, but his offensive skillset remains very vanilla beyond banging home a few goals around the net.

I'm not too worried about his being undersized, but he'll have to become a strong defensive forward — potentially a penalty killer — to stick. He's going to have to fight for a spot in training camp and, if he makes it, fight to hold it. If he can play a responsible game, then he'll be a fan favorite on a fourth line with enough versatility to move higher up the lineup when necessary.

Chrenko is a center who played a prominent role for Slovak league champions HK Nitra in 2025-26 and also shone at the World Junior Championships with eight points in five games. That production alone suggests a player who belongs in the 30th-60th pick range of the NHL draft.

The diminutive forward is one I'd describe as quick rather than fast. Good acceleration and an ability to stop and then get moving without much wasted motion. He has decent speed when carrying wide against defenders. His most dependable trait is his ability to sidestep pressure. You won't see him churn and burn over long distances, though. At least, not in a way that separates him from the pack.

Chrenko has a quality wrist shot. It's quick off his stick. He is good at receiving passes in his wheelhouse. The efficiency in his shooting motion also creates some surprising range in how far out he can score. There is equal parts playmaking ability.

The big questions are the physical aspects and his defensive play. He's 5'11", but he plays even smaller. He's not strong enough to hold his own in battles, and although his agility allows him to skirt around pressure on open ice, he hasn't yet figured out how to avoid getting pinned along the walls. He'll also need to bulk up (he will) and add some resilience when defenders are draped around him.

Defensively, Chrenko puts in effort and has a disruptive stick when pressuring pucks, but he often loses his coverages while switching his visuals between following his check and tracking the puck's movement.

Can he make the NHL and, if so, will he stick at center? There is legitimate doubt for both questions. The Rangers have plenty of high floor, low-upside forwards in the organization so Chrenko, despite reasonable skepticism, is a breath of fresh air. If he makes it, he will be an impact top-nine scoring forward. You can't ask for much more than that at 81st overall.

Garand is 6'1 ", which would traditionally be considered on the smaller side for an NHL goaltender, but that's in the sweet spot for former Rangers goaltending coach Benoit Allaire.

He is mobile in the crease and polished in his movements. He doesn't have a ton of power in his pushes off the post or across the crease, but he compensates well with his mechanics and depth. He anticipates movements to the weak side and consistently gets across in time. Garand has bought into Allaire's insistence on compensating for lack of size by staying on his edges to maximize top-of-net coverage while maintaining mobility. When all else fails, he has innate compete to make desperation saves.

Garand's AHL numbers (.896 save percentage last season) don't do him justice. The Wolf Pack were absolutely atrocious. He was piled on. That NHL veteran, Spencer Martin, posted a .873 save percentage on the same team, which offers perspective on just how well Garand played.

And he's mentally tuned. Rangers fans saw this in his brief NHL spell last season. He was undaunted by the moment behind a less-than-stellar Rangers defense and was absolute nails against the Winnipeg Jets in a 35-save NHL debut.

I don't understand what the Rangers' plan is. While it's understandable that they want insurance at the backup position, the investment in Jonas Korpisalo feels like overkill. Garand has done everything he needs to justify a chance as an NHL backup. He is waiver-eligible this season, and I imagine there's a good chance another team will claim him if they decide to go with Korpisalo. That would be a waste of a good goaltending prospect.

The last pick of the second round this past summer, Ben MacBeath represents good value at 64th overall. One Eastern Conference scout I spoke with had him ranked 45th on his board.

The base of MacBeath's game is his skating, which will be a breath of fresh air to Rangers fans tired of seeing a slow defense. He glides around the ice, pivots strongly in both directions, and can stop quickly from top speed or accelerate rapidly from a standstill. Offensively, he does a pretty good job of weaving the skating into his possessions. The Calgary Hitmen defenseman escapes pressure behind the goal line and starts breakouts by carrying the puck up ice.

MacBeath is someone to start plays but is not really a major executor up the ice. He has pretty good vision and the legs to activate in the offensive zone, but he's not a real quarterback at the blue line and has average shooting and passing ability. His numbers in the WHL are projectable, though: 51 points in 67 games last season.

Defensively, MacBeath has a lot to learn. He can get a bit frantic in defensive coverages, often reactive rather than proactive. I've seen him freeze up with indecision when figuring out what coverage to pick up as a puck moves across the zone or behind the net.

This scouting report sounds more negative than positive so far, but here's the deal: He is a very gifted player. A 6'2" defenseman with excellent skating mechanics is an appetizing starting point. He heads to the University of Denver this season, where he'll be coached by prodigy David Carle. It is unequivocally the ideal landing spot for a talented defenseman who needs a hockey education.

He'll need two, maybe three years in the NCAA before turning pro, but the Rangers have to be thrilled with this development plan, and he could come out the other side as a future second-pairing NHL defenseman.

It was a better sophomore season for Emery, albeit still underwhelming.

The 2024 first-round pick was drafted for his skating and physicality. That much of his game remains present. He's nice to watch when he's moving around the ice. Crossovers and pivots look effortless. He has another gear when it's a race. He also has good footwork when moving while in defense.

Physically, I think he plays a heavier style than he gets credit for. He is not hesitant to battle around the net, fighting for positioning and shoving the shaft of his stick into the back of the net-front presence. He does need to get stronger. His reported 185-pound weight is well below where he should be as a 6'3" shutdown defenseman.

And although he took some steps this season (and really showed it at the end of the season), Emery remains largely a non-factor offensively. He will use his speed to activate in the offensive zone but his puck skills are lacking and his vision and decision-making are a work in progress.

In a redraft of 2024, Emery slips into the second round. He still remains an intriguing prospect. The size-and-speed combination is too interesting to give up on for someone who turned 20 in May. He really needs to get going this next season as a junior at North Dakota in order to trend towards an NHL career as a No 4 defenseman.

The Rangers were fortunate to grab Spence at 43rd overall in 2025 — I thought he should have gone around 35th — and he reaffirmed that perspective as a freshman at the University of Michigan last season. Granted, much of his production came early in the season against weak competition. Twenty percent of his 25 points came in two games against Mercyhurst. He went cold mid-season but, to his credit, played some of his best hockey in tournament play to end the season.

Spence offers visceral appeal. As a winger, he has high-end north-south speed, a major motor, and a spicy attitude. These traits, which served him well in the OHL, absolutely translated immediately in college hockey. He's an effective forechecker; he gets pucks out of his own end through sheer determination, and he beats defensemen to the net.

My previous criticism of his game was that his offensive style was "vanilla." He got on the scoresheet thanks to his speed and work ethic, but at the NHL level that limited his upside. I still think that largely holds true, but he made some meaningful improvements. He has a bit of soft skill and unpredictability to his game now: give-and-go passing sequences, a willingness to try to stickhandle through a defender, the occasional backdoor seam pass.

I still see him as a future NHL third liner, but we're talking about the type who really stands out. A top penalty killer and forechecker with 35-40 points and maybe an 'A' on his sweater. If he continues to develop his soft skills, there may even be a chance he could bump up to a second-line trajectory. Talk of NHL futures is almost always hypothetical for prospects, and less than 20% of second-round picks go on to play 500-plus NHL games. I think Spence's odds are at least ten percentage points higher than that.

Acquired in the Vincent Trocheck trade, Cole Beaudoin was the 24th-overall selection in the 2024 NHL Draft.

He is, primarily, a fierce competitor. It does not matter who is on the ice, in what situation, or in what league. He's not going to get outworked. The effort he puts in to get up ice or back in transition makes him a major asset on the forecheck and defensively.

He's also incredibly strong. He plays through contact and can skate at full speed while staying balanced on his skates. He doesn't get knocked off his puck easily, and he shows incredible leverage when he widens his stance and gets low in board battles. Beaudoin is also excellent on faceoffs.

While he doesn't have superlative skill, he's put in a lot of work to accentuate his abilities to become more of a threat. His skating, once a notable liability, has averaged out and he now has something of a separation gear in open ice against slower defenders, though his stride is still inefficient and choppy.

He has a nice wrist shot, and his catch-and-release is good enough to beat goaltenders in motion. He plays at a high tempo but isn't frenetic with the puck and shows some spatial awareness when carrying it through the neutral zone, finding paths around traffic.

Beaudoin likely peaks as a depth player, but he has a really high floor as a special type of support piece. I like his odds of turning into a 200-foot third-line center who becomes a forechecking machine, creates via cycle offense, never takes a shift off, and scores the occasional shorthanded goal.

Greentree is 6'3" and 216 pounds and is the organization's top prospect when it comes to pure, raw skill. That includes fifth-overall pick Alberts Šmits.

He wants the puck on his stick, and he will drive possessions. Despite lacking foot speed, he creates zone entries with vision, stickhandling, and a long reach that makes it hard for defenders to take the puck off him. He may not be an overly physical player in terms of hitting, but he does not shy away from contact and will operate in open ice.

It really is that combination of reach, stick skills, and vision that makes him such an offensive threat. If he has the size advantage, he'll keep pucks away from his body to create space to move around the offensive zone and find a shooting or passing lane. Yet if a bigger player tries to jump in, he'll pull the puck inside and get around the defender that way. His wrist shot is very good, and he is equally strong as a passer across the slot line.

Success will come down to improving his pace of play. Right now, he is a killer at slow tempos. With time and space to make things happen, he'll get it done. As he moves up to pro hockey next season, he'll have less of that. He needs to improve his acceleration and top speed.

It's also about mixing in different tempos of execution. It can't always be about using the entire 24-second shot clock, metaphorically speaking. Quicker puck execution will prevent pro defenses from skating him into traps and add another element of uncertainty, allowing him to sometimes operate at a slower pace when it best suits the situation.

Greentree should get at least a full year in the NHL and, if all goes well, he may earn a game or two in 2026-2027 before really challenging for a top-nine spot in September 2027. He has second-line upside as an offensive winger who features on the top PP unit and produces 20-25 goals and 30-35 assists.

I wrote a sizable scouting report on Šmits after the 2026 Draft. I'm not going to be able to outdo that effort here. I recommend checking out that piece for a deeper look at Šmits.

Here are the cliff notes: He's big and fast. He eats up a lot of ice. He plays a physical and aggressive game. Sometimes his aggressive decisions get him in trouble, but coaches will appreciate his ambition and work with him to maintain a confident game while picking his spots.

He's a huge asset in a rush offense, beating his checks up the ice to create numerical advantages for his team. He has a hard shot, but he isn't a true quarterback from the blue line and won't manipulate defenses. He has a very high floor in the NHL — it's very tough to see him as anything less than a strong second-pairing defenseman — and his physical tools and determination are so alluring that one can imagine him figuring it all out and becoming a dominant, 25-minute needle-mover.

The path the Rangers and Šmits choose for the near future will be very interesting. He's not far from being NHL-ready, even at 18, but the Rangers have been burned by rushing prospects in the past. There also is no obvious spot on the NHL roster for him at the moment. Do they keep him around to start the season anyway? Does he go to the AHL? Or do they send the Latvian back across the Atlantic to Finland's Liiga?

One Europe-based NHL scout I spoke with compared him to Washington's Jakob Chychrun.

"I think there's legit top-pair upside. Second-best defenseman in the (2026) draft for me," the scout said.

The Rangers' success in selecting fifth overall won't only come down to which player they took but also to the steps that followed in that player's development. Smits can become a big-time player but it can't be taken for granted.

articles.title: Kyler Murray's Status for Vikings vs. Bears Updated in New NFL Rumors amid Injury Recovery
articles.summary: There is reportedly a chance Kyler Murray could play Sunday against the Chicago Bears despite suffering an injury in the season opener against the Green Bay Packers.
articles.body:
There is reportedly a chance Kyler Murray could play Sunday against the Chicago Bears despite suffering an injury in the season opener against the Green Bay Packers.

ESPN's Dan Graziano reported Friday the Minnesota Vikings quarterback is progressing through concussion protocol and "did more in practice Thursday than Wednesday." If and when he is cleared, the Vikings will then have to choose between starting him or sticking with Carson Wentz for at least one more game.

Murray, who was limited to just five games last season for the Arizona Cardinals, was one of Minnesota's key additions this offseason and won the starting job over J.J. McCarthy.

However, he threw just five passes against the Packers before suffering the head injury in the first quarter. Wentz, who was named the backup quarterback over McCarthy, was thrust into action and directed an impressive comeback.

Despite trailing 22-10 in the third quarter, the Vikings ended up defeating Green Bay 39-22.

Wentz completed 12 of his 19 passes for 133 yards, three touchdowns and zero interceptions while the Minnesota defense held the Packers to just three points after halftime.

"That's why he's here," Vikings head coach Kevin O'Connell told reporters when discussing Wentz. "For him to come in and do what he did and just be part of that calming presence that allowed our team to continue playing, I can't say enough about him."

Having an experienced option like Wentz who played well in the season opener gives the Vikings a solid insurance policy should Murray not be ready to face the Bears. They could also play things safe and use more caution with Murray after his setback and wait until Week 3 against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

Chicago is coming off its own win over the Carolina Panthers in its season opener, although either Murray or Wentz will be facing a defense that looked vulnerable in the 59-37 contest.

articles.body:
Kyler Murray will miss Sunday's game against the Chicago Bears as he continues to recover from a concussion suffered during the Minnesota Vikings' Week 1 win over the Green Bay Packers.

ESPN's Dan Graziano reported Friday that Murray is progressing through concussion protocol and "did more in practice Thursday than Wednesday," which suggested he at least had a chance of returning on Sunday.

Murray, who was limited to just five games last season for the Arizona Cardinals, was one of Minnesota's key additions this offseason and won the starting job over J.J. McCarthy.

He threw just five passes against the Packers before suffering the head injury in the first quarter. Carson Wentz, who was named the backup quarterback over McCarthy, was thrust into action and directed an impressive comeback.

Despite trailing 22-10 in the third quarter, the Vikings ended up defeating Green Bay 39-22.

Wentz completed 12 of his 19 passes for 133 yards, three touchdowns and zero interceptions while the Minnesota defense held the Packers to just three points after halftime.

"That's why he's here," Vikings head coach Kevin O'Connell told reporters when discussing Wentz. "For him to come in and do what he did and just be part of that calming presence that allowed our team to continue playing, I can't say enough about him."

Wentz will be under center again Sunday with Murray tracking to return as early as Week 3 against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

articles.title: Tom Cruise Says Taylor Swift Was 'Schooling' Him on Football During Travis Kelce, Chiefs vs. Broncos
articles.summary: Tom Cruise says Taylor Swift was showing off her football knowledge in their shared suite Monday at the Kansas City Chiefs' season-opening win over the visiting Denver Broncos.
articles.body:
Tom Cruise says Taylor Swift was showing off her football knowledge in their shared suite Monday at the Kansas City Chiefs' season-opening win over the visiting Denver Broncos.

Swift and Cruise were spotted sitting together as Swift's husband Travis Kelce made three catches for 71 yards in the Chiefs' 31-10 victory.

"She was schooling me on football. For real," Cruise told Jimmy Fallon in a Thursday appearance on The Tonight Show (4:45 mark of the video below).

Cruise continued, "First of all, she's a genius... she knows her stuff."

Swift, who married Kelce in July, has been a regular attendee at Chiefs games since she and Kelce confirmed their relationship in 2023.

"She knew nothing about football when she met Travis... she knows. She's just bringing it," Cruise said.

Cruise also appeared on a Friday episode of Kelce's New Heights podcast, in which Kelce also complimented his wife's football knowledge.

"Now she knows everything," Kelce said. "She sees the flags coming in, like, 'Oh, that might be a defensive hold...' She's like, 'That's encroachment.' I'm like, 'You know what that is?'"

Kelce's strong start to his age-37 season, along with a dominant Chiefs debut from Kenneth Walker III, helped Patrick Mahomes lead the Chiefs to victory in his return from the knee injury that prematurely ended his 2025 campaign.

Swift could potentially be in attendance again as the Chiefs look to build on that start with another home game Sunday at 8:20 p.m. ET against the visiting Indianapolis Colts.

articles.title: Union Jack Classic: Kansas Jayhawks to face Arizona State Sun Devils in college football's debut at Wembley Stadium
articles.summary: The Kansas Jayhawks face the Arizona State Sun Devils in the inaugural Union Jack Classic at Wembley Stadium on Saturday; watch Week Two of the NFL season on Sky Sports, with five matches live on Sunday
articles.body:
Football is no stranger to international expansion having seen the NFL host regular-season games in London since 2007, while Ireland serves as the home of the annual College Football Classic at the Aviva Stadium in Dublin.

In fact, college football spread its wings long before now having also previously played games in Tokyo and Milan in the 1980s, as well as famously heading to Tanzania for the 2011 Kilimanjaro Bowl.

From its staple marching bands to its iconic tailgates to its deep-rooted family tribalism, the college game is now primed to showcase its unique make-up with the inaugural Union Jack Classic.

"I think I've probably had fish and chips four times since I've been here so it's been a nice culture shock," says Arizona State punter Nick McLarty.

McLarty is perhaps more accustomed to a change in environment more so than any player arriving in the UK this week having grown up in Melbourne, Australia, the 6ft 7in punter having started out playing Aussie Rules before turning his talents to a different kind of football.

"It's my first time coming to London," he said." It's funny, I was on the phone with mum before and actually didn't tell her so the first time she found out was this morning. It's been a lot of fun.

"I have a brother who is pretty big into soccer and when he found out I was playing at Wembley he was beside himself and it's been fun going round to Buckingham Palace.

"The people and the accent [has been a nice change], I've been so used to the American accent, it's been a nice touch of reality for what the rest of the world is like to be able to speak to other people."

Wembley is expected to welcome 60,000 fans this weekend as both teams arrive 1-1 on the season, Kansas coming off a 38-21 defeat to Missouri on Friday night and the Sun Devils having just lost 48-20 to Texas A&M.

For many of the players it represents their first time leaving the US, Kansas head coach Lance Leipold having described it as a "lifetime" opportunity.

Leipold had notably been a graduate assistant for Wisconsin when the Badgers featured in the Coca-Cola Classic in Tokyo back in 1993.

"[That] is when you really get to think about what you did, and something that you talk about with your friends and team-mates for a lifetime. And that's partially what I'm hoping for," Leipold said this week.

"I think even though we have so many things going on in college athletics, that we should not take away experiences such as this if they're afforded to you, and try to make the most of it. I think it's something that we're looking forward to."

The pre-game tailgate is scheduled to kickstart festivities at 10am along Wembley Way, with 15,000 fans flying over from the US to contribute to what is hoped to be a classic college football atmosphere.

"I grew up playing soccer, one of my old coaches who played for Everton always talked about playing at Wembley and scoring a goal there so it's kind of a full circle moment really," said Sun Devils defensive lineman Zac Swanson.

"It's super cool and we're really blessed to be here. It took a little bit to get adjusted to the time, it's probably one of our better weeks because back in Arizona it's 115 degrees out and now we get to practise in 70s so preparation is going very well.

"It's almost like a whole culture shock because it's so different. My favourite thing is the houses and environment, you see the soccer pitches everywhere, we don't really have that in the US."

Former NFL quarterback Robert Griffin III will be in London as part of the Fox Sports team presenting live their pre-game show live from the UK.

He explained what makes college football's atmosphere and environment special.

"The fandom around college football is better," he told media. "It just is. The traditions and all that stuff are definitely more deep-rooted. The rivalries are better than the NFL rivalries and I just think it adds to it.

"There is no NFL without college and there's no college football without the NFL.

"You actually sink your roots deeper into the ground by becoming a college football fan so you can truly follow these guys," Griffin said. "That jersey that you put on, that you buy, that you spend all your hard-earned money on actually means more to you because you've been following those players longer."

articles.title: Why Buffalo Bills played the Canadian national anthem
articles.summary: The field in Buffalo was decked out with the flags of both countries, as tensions simmer and a trade war escalates.
articles.body:
There are no Canadian teams in the NFL - but there are millions of fans.

At the Buffalo Bills game in New York on Thursday night, plenty of Canadians wore the team's trademark red, white and blue while drinking beside their pick-up trucks, which were parked to tailgate - a very American pre-game tradition.

The Bills' stadium is only 112 miles (180 km) from Toronto - about a two and a half hour drive for fans - and right across Lake Ontario, which President Donald Trump has sought to rename Lake America.

So it was no surprise that many Canadians arrived long before kick-off to soak up the atmosphere and enjoy the sights of the new Highmark Stadium for their team 's home opener against the Detroit Lions.

What was unusual was that their national anthem rang out through the stadium.

The field was decked out with both the stars and stripes of the US flag and the maple leaf of the Canadian one, and the 1990s Canadian band The Barenaked Ladies belted out Oh Canada! in front of a massive crowd.

It was an emotional moment for many of the Canadian fans, who said they felt an extremely warm welcome even if their country's mood has recently grown more frosty towards the US.

"I've always felt welcome here," said Ben Kerr, from Bradford, Ontario.

"I think it's a nice acknowledgement," he added. "I appreciate that the Bills are doing that for Canada."

The relationship between the two countries, which began to sour when US President Donald Trump returned to office and made repeated calls to annex Canada, has frayed further with an escalating tit-for-tat tariff showdown.

Prime Minister Mark Carney has said Canada, which shares the world's longest undefended border with the US, is "at war" with its southern neighbour over trade. Trump has called Canada "nasty" and "entitled".

Both sides are feeling the economic impact, with Canadian industries reeling from tariffs and Canadians boycotting travel and spending in the US.

The ongoing tensions made the decision to travel to Buffalo a little more complicated for Kerr.

"I try to spend as little money as possible in the US," he told the BBC. "Buy our food in Canada, buy our beer in Canada, bring it across and drink it here. We're not big in supporting the American economy in this trade war."

Canadians dream of Europe as Carney floats longshot plan for living and working in EU

Trump signs order to rename Lake Ontario as Lake America

EU chief backs plan for Canada to become 'associate member'

Many Americans at the game expressed their own frustrations with the escalating trade war, and the way it has divided the two neighbours.

For Drew Grier, an American who lives eight minutes from the stadium, "the anthem playing tonight is a core part of who we are as a border city".

At a Buffalo Sabres playoff ice hockey game in April, a microphone died while the Canadian anthem was being sung and the audience's voices filled in.

"You sang the Canadian anthem because it needed to happen," Grier said.

Canadian Blake Parnham recalled that moment: "I was sobbing watching the game at home because I felt so vindicated, that Buffalo is different."

He couldn't make it to Buffalo for the Bills home opener, but he enjoyed it from his elaborately decorated backyard in Keswick, Ontario.

Grier said that singing the Canadian anthem tonight is "not that polarising of a thing".

"If anyone is polarising it, it's coming from those outside here, because those of us here, we love Canada," he said.

"The only acceptable reason to sing that anthem would be if they were playing a Canadian team, but they don't play any Canadian teams," posted one fan on social media.

"I don't think it's really necessary," said David Waring, who attended Thursday's game.

Many Canadians are boycotting the US, so this is where they're travelling instead

In the end, it may all come down to simple economics.

The Bills' new home, Highmark Stadium, cost $2.2bn to build. While the population of western New York is a little over 1.5 million, the nearby Toronto and Hamilton greater metro areas is home to more than 8 million. Simply put, the team needs Canadian fans.

Gavin Kemp, who has run the NFL-Canada office for eight years, told the BBC that Canada's relationship to the NFL was "extremely important".

Asked why the Bills chose this year to play the Canadian anthem, Kemp said the team was "leaning into one of their biggest parts of their market".

Canada boasts nearly 15 million NFL fans – about one-third of the country's population, and roughly 10-15% of Bills season ticket holders are Canadian, according to the team.

"Sports really transcends all of this," Kemp said. "All this politics is kind of secondary to the fact that your team is doing fantastic right now."

Even American fans who traditionally cheer for other teams found themselves siding with the Bills.

Carol Breed, who backs the Detroit Lions, considered travelling to Highmark Stadium from her home in Battle Creek, Michigan, after she heard they would play the Canadian national anthem.

"I love our country's relationship with Canada," the 74-year-old told the BBC, adding that in Michigan the country is viewed more as a "relative".

"I just hate what Trump has done to the partnership."

She wasn't able to watch the game in person, but has found other ways to scratch her O'Canada itch.

A couple of weeks ago, Breed embarked on the two-hour drive across the border, on the recently opened Gordie Howe International Bridge , which has also stoked divisions between the two nations of late.

"We sang the US anthem until we reached halfway and then started singing the Canadian anthem," she said.

Canadians welcome closer ties with Europe as tensions simmer with US

What's going on between the US and Canada?

'Everything on the table' including retaliation as Canada plans response to US tariffs

Out of that travel that spanned continents, we're getting a picture of his plans for league expansion. Bottom line: Goodell sees NFL expansion outside the United States on the horizon.
