articles.title: Cowboys' Jerry Jones Addresses Possibility of Tinting AT&T Stadium's Windows After FIFA World Cup
articles.summary: Testing out tinted windows during the 2026 FIFA World Cup games at AT&T Stadium apparently didn't convince Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones any changes need to be made when the stadium hosts NFL games.
articles.body:
Testing out tinted windows during the 2026 FIFA World Cup games at AT&T Stadium apparently didn't convince Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones any changes need to be made when the stadium hosts NFL games.

"I really don't know about that at all," Jones said when asked in a Friday appearance on 105.3 The Fan if he planned to tint windows again for Sunday's home opener against the Washington Commanders. "So, no, not necessarily."

Jones added, "No, I don't think so. I don't know of any plans to surprise our fans."

The Cowboys' home stadium is built with its end zones pointing east and west, an orientation that allows the sun to shine through the windows on the west side of the stadium during afternoon games.

AT&T Stadium addressed the issue by tinting those windows ahead of a World Cup match at the venue in June, per Nick Harris of the Fort Worth Star-Telegram.

Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer joked in June he would "miss the experience" of seeing the stadium featuring both tinted windows and a grass field this summer.

Wide receiver CeeDee Lamb, who has been calling for years for the Cowboys to block the sunlight coming into the stadium, said last week on Caleb Downs' Downs 2 Business podcast he thought some changes might be coming to the stadium windows in the near future.

"I think they're gonna put some tint," Lamb said around the 18:50 mark of the podcast. "I think they're going to put tint on the glass now, so we'll see."

Schottenheimer then said he felt like "anything's possible" when asked about the potential tint in his own Friday appearance on 105.3 The Fan.

It sounds like Schottenheimer and Lamb could be back to battling sun glare when the Cowboys kick off their home opener Sunday at 4:25 p.m. ET against the Washington Commanders.

articles.title: Cooper Rush Will Start for Falcons vs. Panthers amid Tua Tagovailoa, Penix Injuries
articles.summary: The Atlanta Falcons will start Cooper Rush at quarterback for the second straight week.
articles.body:
The Atlanta Falcons will start Cooper Rush at quarterback for the second straight week.

Ian Rapoport of ESPN and NFL Network and The Athletic's Jonathan Jones previously reported the news.

Tua Tagovailoa didn't practice Thursday because of an oblique injury, and Michael Penix Jr. isn't yet in full game shape following his long recovery from an ACL tear.

Penix said Wednesday he's "close" to feeling ready to play.

"I know I've been saying that, but there's just a couple of technical things that I want to hit, some goals that I have that I want to achieve before I do stuff out on that field," he said. "But I do feel really good, and we're taking strides each and every day."

With Rush getting the nod, Jack Strand will presumably occupy the backup role once again in Week 2.

Rush, who had started in place of an injured Dak Prescott at times for the Dallas Cowboys, had a forgettable showing in Atlanta's opener. He went 12-of-22 for 143 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions in a 20-13 loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers.

Perhaps Week 2 presents a more favorable matchup. The Carolina Panthers got torched to the tune of 59 points and 552 total yards by the Chicago Bears in Week 1.

This may not be a good time to cross paths with the Panthers defense, though, as they'll have a lot of frustration to release on the field.

Should Rush deliver another lackluster showing, the Falcons will hope Penix or Tagovailoa is cleared because otherwise it might be worth considering Strand.

articles.title: Terry Bradshaw reveals why Nick Saban had enough at Alabama as NIL turned college football into a new game
articles.summary: NFL News: Terry Bradshaw has offered his view on why Nick Saban walked away from Alabama, saying the former coach did not want to spend his final years dealing .
articles.body: Terry Bradshaw has offered his view on why Nick Saban walked away from Alabama, saying the former coach did not want to spend his final years dealing with the new demands of college football. Bradshaw said Saban did not want to keep recruiting his own players because of NIL money and the transfer portal. Saban retired on January 10, 2024, after 17 seasons at Alabama.Terry Bradshaw explains Nick Saban’s Alabama retirementBradshaw shared his view during an appearance on The Buddy Martin Show. He pointed to one part of modern college football that he believes Saban simply did not want to keep dealing with.“I think Nick Saban left Alabama because he didn’t want to do that,” Bradshaw said. “Look, you don’t want to have to continue to recruit your players that you’ve already signed year after year after year.”Bradshaw was talking about the growing role of money in college football. With NIL deals and the transfer portal changing how rosters are built, coaches now have to spend more time keeping players, finding replacements and dealing with financial questions.Saban had already spoken openly about those changes before leaving Alabama. He criticized NIL deals that he felt were being used as a way to attract players and questioned the effects of the transfer portal.Still, Saban’s own comments show that retirement was not presented as being caused by one issue alone. When he announced his decision, he said he believed it was time to walk away. He also pointed to changes around NIL, transfers, tampering and the recruiting calendar.Nick Saban, NIL and the changes at AlabamaSaban’s retirement came nine days after Alabama lost to Michigan in the Rose Bowl. ESPN reported that he told his players the changes in college football had helped him decide that the time was right to retire.His record at Alabama made the decision a major moment. Saban won six national championships with the Crimson Tide and seven overall, including one at LSU. He finished his Alabama run with a 201 29 record.The NIL issue has not disappeared from Saban’s life since he left coaching. He has continued to speak about how college sports should be managed, and in 2026 he became a public supporter of the Protect College Sports Act.The bill, introduced by Senators Maria Cantwell and Ted Cruz, would create federal rules for NIL deals, transfers, recruiting and other parts of college athletics. It also includes a revenue sharing framework and protections for women’s and Olympic sports. The Senate advanced the bill in September, but it still requires further action before it can become law.Saban has also appeared in a $10 million advertising campaign supporting the bill alongside Deion Sanders. The campaign argues that college sports need clearer national rules.Bradshaw’s explanation focuses on the daily work of keeping a modern roster together, while Saban’s own statements show that he had serious concerns about the wider changes taking place around college football. The two views point to the same major shift without proving that NIL alone caused Saban to retire.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Cowboys' Schottenheimer Reacts to Viral Visor Meme, Explains Using Different Colored Pens in Games
articles.summary: Dallas Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer says he might invest in a multi-colored pen after the multiple writing implements tucked into his visor drew attention during last Sunday's season-opening loss at the New York Giants.
articles.body:
Dallas Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer says he might invest in a multi-colored pen after the multiple writing implements tucked into his visor drew attention during last Sunday's season-opening loss at the New York Giants.

Schottenheimer told reporters Friday his daughter had sent him memes referencing his storage technique, including an AI image of his head covered in pens he described as "a little overdone."

"I am going to get one of those pens that's got the multicolors, you know, where you can go red, brown," Schottenheimer said. "I've got a lot of stuff in my pockets. I've got a red flag I've got to carry... maybe I'll just make [chief of staff] Tyler Boyles stand next to me and hold all my pens."

He added that he uses different colors to mark plays that have already been called versus plays he plans to call later in the game.

Schottenheimer has been walking the Cowboys sidelines with pens tucked beneath his visor since taking over as head coach ahead of the 2025 season.

He said last year he saw his visor as somewhat of an ode to College Football Hall of Fame coach Steve Spurrier, who he played for at Florida in the late '90s.

Schottenheimer is looking to lead the Cowboys back into the playoffs after a 7-9-1 finish to his first season as the helm. He'll look to start that push by bouncing back from Week 1's loss during Sunday's home opener against the visiting Washington Commanders.

articles.title: 49ers Distributed 'Fly Kits,' Sleep Plans to Players for Australia Flight, Full Details Revealed
articles.summary: The San Francisco 49ers tried to leave no stone unturned to prepare their players for the long flight to Australia for the 2026 season opener.
articles.body:
The San Francisco 49ers tried to leave no stone unturned to prepare their players for the long flight to Australia for the 2026 season opener.

The MMQB's Albert Breer documented the Niners' journey and reported members of the team received "fly kits" as they boarded their plane. The packet included sleep supplements and "a detailed schedule on when to take them to help reset each player's circadian rhythm."

Staffers also suggested following one of two rest strategies. Players could stay awake for a few hours and then sleep in one big chunk or sleep for a few hours at a time with a break in between.

"We tried to stay up until it was like 4 or 5 a.m. our time," fullback Kyle Juszczyk told Breer. "And we were all exhausted at that point, so it was pretty easy to fall asleep. And with the different things they gave us, like the melatonin, I was actually able to stay asleep for a good 9–10 hours. Then I woke up, I had like an hour left, ate breakfast, and had this circadian reset supplement with pomegranate extract in it or something.

"I took that and had a lot of caffeine."

Juszczyk also estimated he needed "about three days" to shake off all of the jet lag from the trip. That left him with plenty of time to mentally and physically recover before San Francisco played the Los Angeles Rams.

As NFL fans are well aware by now, the Rams took the exact opposite approach. They touched down in Australia as close as realistically possible before the game.

The Niners came away a 27-7 winner, leading more people to wonder whether L.A. outsmarted itself.

The Athletic's Mike Sando interviewed sports scientists who "said the Rams were spot-on in their handling of the sleep component, but they risked players feeling heavy-legged because it takes time for fluid buildup in the legs to dissipate following such a long flight."

That was all the more notable because Rams star Myles Garrett suffered a knee injury that landed him on injured reserve.

The NFL will be returning to Australia at some point, though no future game is confirmed. When that happens, the teams making the trek are likely to follow the blueprint laid out by the 49ers.

articles.title: Anthony Richardson Suffers Injury Lifting Weights, Latest Updates on Colts QB's Status for Week 2
articles.summary: Despite missing practice Tuesday, Indianapolis Colts quarterback Anthony Richardson avoided a significant injury.
articles.body:
Despite missing practice Tuesday, Indianapolis Colts quarterback Anthony Richardson avoided a significant injury.

Colts head coach Shane Steichen said Friday that while Richardson tweaked his groin muscle lifting weights this week, he is healthy and will remain the team's backup quarterback for Sunday's contest against the Kansas City Chiefs, per James Boyd of The Athletic.

Daniel Jones will remain the starter, while Riley Leonard is in the third-string role.

It has been some time since Richardson, who entered the league as the No. 4 overall pick of the 2023 NFL draft, has taken meaningful snaps. While he started four games as a rookie and 11 games in 2024, he did not record a single start last season and threw just two total passes.

This surely isn't the role the Colts envisioned when they used a top-five draft pick on him with the idea he would eventually become their franchise quarterback.

Alas, he struggled in 2024 when given the chance to be the team's full-time starter and completed just 47.7 percent of his passes for 1,814 yards, eight touchdowns and 12 interceptions. He did add 499 yards and six touchdowns on the ground as a runner, but the struggles in the aerial attack stood out.

Ideally for Indianapolis, Jones will remain healthy and thrive after leading the team to an 8-5 record in his 13 starts last season before he suffered a torn Achilles.

Yet if there are any issues against the Chiefs, Richardson will be ready to take over as needed despite a minor setback leading up to the game.

articles.title: Jeremiyah Love Says Cardinals Have Asked Him for Scouting Report on Jadarian Price's 'Weaknesses'
articles.summary: The Arizona Cardinals turned to running back Jeremiyah Love to get whatever edge they could while planning to face his former college teammate Jadarian Price.
articles.body:
The Arizona Cardinals turned to running back Jeremiyah Love to get whatever edge they could while planning to face his former college teammate Jadarian Price.

"They've been asking me stuff like, 'What are some of his weaknesses?' Stuff like that," Love said, per Pro Football Talk's Michael David Smith . "J doesn't have many weaknesses. If you can get him you got to get him. Once he gets the ball, he gets rolling. It's hard to stop him. He's real fast. . . . You've got to get him early. I think very highly of JD, so I don't really know what to say. Got to get him. Get him before he gets rolling."

Love and Price were on the Fighting Irish together for three seasons. The former played a starring role, with the latter delivering strong numbers as the secondary option on the ground.

Price proceeded to make a nice impression in his first game with the Seattle Seahawks. He carried the ball 10 times for 52 yards in a 13-10 win over the New England Patriots.

His usage could tick upward with Seattle quarterback Sam Darnold missing practice on Wednesday and Thursday because of a glute injury. The coaching staff has had plenty of advance warning to draw up a scheme with a heavier emphasis on the running game if need be.

Unless they're planning to deploy him at linebacker, Love's knowledge of Price probably won't go that far for the Cardinals.

articles.title: “Not Falling for This Propaganda”: NFL Fans Doubt Josh Allen Played With Flu and Needed IVs Before TNF Game
articles.summary: Michael Jordan’s legendary “Flu Game” during the 1997 NBA Finals came down as one of the greatest moments in sports history. Now, Buffalo Bills quarterback J...
articles.body:
Michael Jordan's legendary "Flu Game" during the 1997 NBA Finals came down as one of the greatest moments in sports history. Now, Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen may have just followed in his footsteps as he led his team to a 41-31 win over the Detroit Lions in Week 2, and according to "Thursday Night Football" analyst Richard Sherman , he did that while battling the flu.

In the postgame interview with Allen, Sherman said that the quarterback was "shivering in a hot tub," needed IVs, and refused to be admitted to a hospital before throwing three touchdown passes and two rushing touchdowns.

Some NFL fans weren't convinced by Sherman's account, with several questioning how the story was presented and the comparisons with Jordan's famous performance.

"Omg I'm not falling for this propaganda," said a fan.

Allen had 20 completions out of 31 attempts for 248 yards against the Lions, with three passing touchdowns plus two rushing touchdowns to complete one of the best performances of his career.

Josh Allen Made History As Bills Played in New Stadium

As the Buffalo Bills finally played in the brand new Highmark Stadium, Josh Allen made history as he extended not just one NFL record but two. The first record is for the most NFL games with at least two passing touchdowns and two rushing touchdowns, and Allen extended his record to 10. The second-most games in the NFL is Steve Young's four.

The second record he extended is the record for the most NFL games with at least three passing touchdowns and two rushing touchdowns. This game would be the fourth such game in his career, with the only other player to do it more than once being Kordell Stewart with two games.

articles.title: Falcons news: Is Atlanta's QB woes proof that Kevin Stefanski is cursed?
articles.summary: The Atlanta Falcons will be facing the Carolina Panthers in Week 2, and there seems to be uncertainty on who will be the quarterback on the field for the gam...
articles.body:
The Atlanta Falcons will be facing the Carolina Panthers in Week 2, and there seems to be uncertainty on who will be the quarterback on the field for the game. Throughout the week, Cooper Rush and Michael Penix Jr. have been splitting first-team reps , but the former didn't play well in Week 1, and the latter still doesn't seem to be ready to come back to the field.

It's been a rough start for the Falcons at quarterback, especially when noting that Tua Tagovailoa was named the starter before Week 1, and his set to miss his second straight game after not practicing this week due to an oblique injury.

People are now looking at head coach Kevin Stefanski and think that he needs to right his wrongs somewhere in order to find some consistency at the position.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

"The nightmare continues for Kevin Stefanski. He must be cursed. He definitely needs to do something and exorcise these demons," Mike Golic Jr . said on his radio show.

"Overall, is it worse than the decades of quarterback situations in Cleveland ? No," Mike Golic Sr. said. But to not know who your quarterback is going to be of the three, is… I mean, you prepare all year long for the start of the season, and just the rug getting pulled out from underneath you, for a team that we thought may struggle anyway, because of a couple of defensive issues. Now, it's pull a name out of a hat to see who's going at quarterback."

This is familiar to what Stefanski had to deal with during his time with the Cleveland Browns , and it felt like he always had a new quarterback every season.

It's uncertain what this situation could look like for the future, but after two weeks, it's not looking good.

articles.title: Cooper Rush to start again at QB for Falcons in Week 2 vs. Panthers; Michael Penix Jr. out, Tua Tagovailoa doubtful
articles.summary: Penix is still ramping back up after recovering from his knee injury, and Tagovailoa has remained sidelined by his oblique issue.
articles.body:
Cooper Rush will start under center again for the Atlanta Falcons this week versus the Carolina Panthers , head coach Kevin Stefanski confirmed Friday .

Michael Penix Jr. is "getting closer" but is "not there yet" in his return to game action, according to NFL Network's Mike Garafolo , in his road back from a partially torn ACL that required season-ending surgery last year . Despite practicing in full, Penix was officially ruled out on Friday, and Tua Tagovailoa — who didn't practice all week — was listed with a "doubtful" designation.

Against the Steelers, Rush threw for 143 yards, 1 touchdown and 2 interceptions on 12-of-22 passing. Notably, his pick 6 early in the fourth quarter afforded the Steelers a two-score lead. Before Pittsburgh's T.J. Watt intercepted that swing pass and took it back to the house , Atlanta trailed by only three points in the final frame.

Rush's lone TD pass came late in the first quarter, when he whipped the ball on a screen to running back Bijan Robinson , who made a bee-line for the end zone, completing the 23-yard score .

Rush, 32, is in his 10th NFL season. The journeyman, originally undrafted out of Central Michigan in 2017, has posted a 9-8 record in 17 career starts. That said, he hasn't won a start since he went 4-4 with the Dallas Cowboys in 2024. Last season, he lost both of the games he started for the Baltimore Ravens , including a Week 6 game against the Los Angeles Rams that saw him benched .

Earlier this week, Stefanski told reporters that he wasn't "ruling anyone out" from his QB room to get the start in Week 2 . That position group includes rookie Jack Strand, a former undrafted free agent who played his college ball at Division II Minnesota State Moorhead but impressed during the preseason.

Rush, though, will get another crack at the QB1 job on Sunday against the Panthers, and Strand will back him up.

articles.title: Ben Johnson vs. Brian Flores: The 'mental war' behind Sunday's chess match in Vikings-Bears
articles.summary: The Ben Johnson-Brian Flores chess match should be another fascinating battle of wits, even if neither of them truly knows what to expect.
articles.body:
Bears QB Caleb Williams did not talk this week like a man coming off a 59-point performance. Facing Vikings defensive coordinator Brian Flores, Williams said — borrowing a phrase from his head coach — is a "mental war."

Flores and Bears head coach Ben Johnson have gone head-to-head six times since 2023. Johnson's side has won five, and four of those victories were 30-plus-point games when Johnson was in Detroit . Last season, Flores' defense held Johnson's offense to 24 and 19 points, with the Vikings beating the Bears in Chicago and losing by two points in the rematch at home.

Sunday's meeting at Soldier Field comes after Johnson and Flores flexed their respective muscles in Week 1. Johnson's Bears rang up 552 yards on the Panthers, including 291 on the ground. Flores' Vikings blitzed the Packers ' Jordan Love into the dirt, with four sacks and 15 QB hits.

Neither the head coach nor coordinator is showing his opponent anything he hasn't seen before — which is exactly the problem. Three years and six meetings in, both men are still finding new ways to make each other guess wrong.

Brian Flores' defense is about far more than hell-bent blitzing

More than anything, Flores' product is uncertainty. Situation and personnel can tell you only so much about his battle plans. Flores will show all-out pressure, then walk out of it. He'll dress a four-man rush in a six-man look. The endgame is the hesitation: Flores wants quarterbacks spending that extra half-second solving a problem, only to find out they're solving the wrong one.

Week 1 was the cranked-up version of Flores' defense. He sent extra rushers at Love on 78.3% of his dropbacks last Sunday, per Next Gen Stats, which was the highest rate any NFL quarterback has seen since 2023. That tape will have been played repeatedly in Lake Forest this week. It is also the tape Flores has completely abandoned against Johnson and Williams.

In two games against the Bears last season, Flores took wildly different approaches. In the Week 1 meeting at Soldier Field, he blitzed on only 37% of the dropbacks. In the Week 11 rematch, that rate shot up to 67%. Williams was held to pedestrian numbers in the two games (55.1% completions, 6.0 yards per attempt), taking two sacks in each game.

"You've got to be able to go out there and [know] bad things are going to happen," Williams said. "You've got to be able to fight back and stay steady. That's one of the biggest things is not allowing his defense and all of that to fluster you and get in your mind."

That pressure disparity reveals what makes Flores dangerous in this matchup: He's not married to any one version of himself. What makes it so hard for Chicago to scout the "real" Flores is that there isn't one. There's only whichever version shows up Sunday.

"You don't [predict what's coming]. You try to have answers for everything," Johnson said. "[Flores has] been in this division three years now, and yeah, I mean, you'd like to think he's put everything he could possibly do on tape until you play him next and you realize he hasn't yet. So it'll be something new. There always is with him, and that's what makes him such a good coordinator."

Which is exactly why Johnson has spent three years building an offense that, he hopes, doesn't need to guess right.

Ben Johnson wants defenses to respect everything but understand little

Whereas Flores' currency is uncertainty, Johnson deals in manufactured indecision: forcing defenses to account for multiple problems to the same pre-snap look. Everything is wrapped up in similar window dressing — condensed splits, motion, under center, tempo.

"There's shifts, there's motions, there's a lot of eye candy," Flores said. "They do everything that could potentially give a defense problems."

But is it run or pass? That's the question Johnson wants a defense asking itself right up until it's too late to answer correctly.

Sunday's explosion was proof of what can happen to a defense that guesses wrong too often. The Bears gutted the Panthers' nickel defense last weekend, and it wasn't all against lighter boxes. Johnson's use of condensed formations and heavy use of "Duo" and outside-zone runs really put Carolina's outside "contain" defenders in a bind. Drawing perimeter defenders toward the ball moves them closer to the players blocking them, with less space to attack downhill, and it forces them to pick a gap before the picture is fully formed.

Off of that, Johnson and Williams can attack with play action, the standard dropback passing game or plays designed to get Williams out in space, where opponents must respect the throw and scramble possibility. It's the same picture for run and pass, and defenses are constantly guessing which one they're actually getting.

A lot of Johnson's offense is built around finding solutions that work against multiple problems, rather than trying to guess what's coming defensively. Johnson wants to prevent defenses from having clean answers to what the Bears present and force defenses to account for every possibility — and he'll try to do it through any and all means possible.

"Any type of offense that's out there — ground-and-pound, run-and-shoot, RPO, 4-by-1 – he's got it," Flores said of Johnson. "So what are we getting this week? It's hard to know. A lot of the game is adjustments. If they do this, we want to do this. We're going to have our own game plan, and it's the same on his end with him asking, 'What are they doing? How are we going to counteract it?'"

It's just as unlikely for Flores to blitz Sunday the way he did against Green Bay as it is for Johnson to run the same blueprint against Minnesota that the Bears ran at Carolina. Both coaches have spent three years building systems designed to deny the other a stable target, which means Sunday isn't really about who has the better plan. It's about who blinks first.

All the game plans and offensive wizardry sound great until there are personnel issues. That's suddenly a concern that could change the outlook for Sunday's game against the Vikings significantly.

Bears RBs D'Andre Swift (ankle, knee) and Kyle Monangai (hamstring) both popped up on the injury list this week, though both returned to full practice on Friday. Right tackle Darnell Wright (knee) was also limited on Thursday before practicing fully Friday. It's fair to say that Chicago's run game won't be operating at full strength if any or all miss the game.

The Vikings also are dealing with injuries on defense, including to linebackers Blake Cashman (wrist) and Andrew Van Ginkel (chest). Both are expected to play, and thankfully for them, Dallas Turner is coming off arguably his best game as a Viking and could be pegged for even more responsibility. The Vikings' defensive front was also a question heading into the season, but it performed well in Week 1.

If the Bears are inclined to throw more, Williams is surrounded by weapons. Rome Odunze has stepped into the WR1 slot and Luther Burden III 's role appears to have grown from Year 1. Tight end Colston Loveland shockingly was shut out in last week's blowout, so you know Johnson wants to get him going. Fellow TE Cole Kmet , who caught a brilliant TD pass last weekend, has more catches against the Vikings than any other team in his career.

The Bears have multiple options to throw to. The Vikings' secondary, which just welcomed back Harrison Smith , is thinner depth-wise but features good experience in Flores' system.

But the Vikings must also prepare for another Bears wrinkle: their touchdown-or-bust mentality. Johnson didn't accidentally say he was taking aim at the league's scoring record, and Week 1 appeared to back up the bravado. Whether it comes from knowing Chicago's defense has its limitations or from Johnson's extreme confidence in his personnel and system, it felt undeniable in Week 1.

"Scoring every drive is our mindset," Williams said. "That's the potential of us. That's an internal expectation, that's an internal feeling just of what we have up front, out wide and in the backfield. It's an expectation from ourselves to be able to go out there and score every time and figure out ways to help the defense."

And it's just another wrinkle to this fantastic chess match between Flores and Johnson. You know it's going to be entertaining, even if you have no idea what to actually expect.

articles.title: Watch Eli Manning, Giants' Jameis Winston Audition for 'Hamilton' Roles in New Video
articles.summary: New York Giants quarterback Jameis Winston took a break from preparing to back up Jaxson Dart to test out his theatrical skills on Broadway.
articles.body:
New York Giants quarterback Jameis Winston took a break from preparing to back up Jaxson Dart to test out his theatrical skills on Broadway.

Winston joined former Giants quarterback Eli Manning and offensive lineman Shaun O'Hara in auditioning for Hamilton in Friday's episode of The Eli Manning Show.

The video showed the quarterbacks learning songs and dances from the hit musical at the Richard Rodgers Theatre in Manhattan.

Winston has been preparing for this audition for years. He started singing a song from Hamilton last season during a Giants press conference.

He also recently posed backstage with cast members after a performance of Hamilton earlier this month.

The Giants signed Winston earlier this month to a two-year extension that will keep him under contract through 2028. He started out this season by backing up Dart in last Sunday's season-opening win over the Dallas Cowboys.

articles.title: Raiders' Fernando Mendoza Explains Wearing Helmet on Sideline While Backing Up Cousins in Week 1
articles.summary: Some fans may have found it a little odd to see Las Vegas Raiders rookie Fernando Mendoza wearing a helmet on the sideline as the backup quarterback, but there was a very practical purpose.
articles.body:
Some fans may have found it a little odd to see Las Vegas Raiders rookie Fernando Mendoza wearing a helmet on the sideline as the backup quarterback, but there was a very practical purpose.

Mendoza told The Athletic's Sam Warren he wanted to hear the communication between coaches and starting QB Kirk Cousins.

"Wearing the helmet is pretty crucial because that's where the play calls come in through, and that's the microphone you hear from the speaker," he said. "When I wear the helmet, I can (experience) what I would actually see on the field."

Somewhat curiously, the No. 1 overall pick said nobody on the Raiders offered to give him a headset or earpiece, which is how backups typically stay engaged.

Even if they had, Mendoza may have preferred the helmet anyway. Warren wrote he's "a firm believer in verbalization" and visualizing what he'd do in a certain situation when watching from afar. He's not sitting idly by as Cousins runs the offense.

"Mendoza says his process observing Cousins on game days is the same as during walkthroughs and practices," per Warren. "He simultaneously mimics Cousins' every action, hearing and saying the play call, then making mock decisions about his throwing progression on passing plays. He even breaks the huddle — a huddle of one — after relaying [coach Klint] Kubiak's call to imaginary teammates."

Mendoza is going to start for the Raiders eventually, and it may happen at some point this season. Whenever the change happens, Kubiak won't have to worry about whether the first-year signal-caller is ready for the promotion.

articles.title: Adam Vinatieri to Attempt Guinness World Records Kick in Swiss Alps Ahead of Patriots' Munich Game
articles.summary: Adam Vinatieri is widely considered one of the greatest kickers of all-time, having made a number of memorable field goals during his time with the New England Patriots and Indianapolis Colts.
articles.body:
Adam Vinatieri is widely considered one of the greatest kickers of all-time, having made a number of memorable field goals during his time with the New England Patriots and Indianapolis Colts.

But he's looking to add a Guinness World Records kick to his resume in retirement.

The Patriots announced Friday that as part of the promotion for its Nov. 15 game against the Detroit Lions in Munich, Germany, Vinatieri will travel to the Swiss Alps to attempt a kick on the Jungfraujoch – Top of Europe.

The plan is for the Patriots and Jungfrau Railways to set up goal posts in the snow for the Hall of Famer to attempt the highest elevation field goal in history.

"I've had the chance to attempt a lot of special kicks in my career, but getting to go for an official Guinness World Records title on snow at 3,454 meters in a Patriots jersey is truly something special," he said. "The conditions up there in the Alps are completely different from anything we know from the NFL. That's exactly what makes this challenge so exciting."

Vinatieri was just inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame as part of the class of 2026. He played 24 seasons, 10 of which came with the Patriots and 14 of which came with the Indianapolis Colts.

While he played more seasons in Indianapolis, he won three of his four Super Bowl rings in New England.

And he might be adding his name to the Guinness World Records while representing the Patriots as well.

articles.title: Vikings QB Kyler Murray ruled out for Week 2 matchup vs. Bears while in concussion protocol
articles.summary: Minnesota coach Kevin O'Connell said Friday that he expects Murray, who left the team's Week 1 win over the Packers after sustaining a scary hit, to be clear...
articles.body:
The Minnesota Vikings will be without Kyler Murray in Week 2, with the starting quarterback officially ruled out of Sunday's matchup against the Chicago Bears due to a concussion.

Murray suffered the injury on Sunday after taking a scary hit in the Vikings ' win over the Green Bay Packers . He was placed in concussion protocol on Monday.

In a news conference on Friday, Minnesota head coach Kevin O'Connell said that Murray had "shown a lot of progress," and that they "fully anticipate him clearing the protocol early next week."

Per the team's injury report, Murray has been limited in practice this week. O'Connell told reporters on Monday that Murray was able to participate in team meetings despite the head injury, and said that they'll "just take it a day at a time."

With Murray out, Carson Wentz will again step up as the team's QB1. Wentz went on to rally Minnesota to victory over the Packers to open the season, thanks in part to some late misfires from Green Bay . J.J. McCarthy will be the backup quarterback, per O'Connell.

Murray, who signed a one-year deal with the Vikings after being released by the Arizona Cardinals in March, started his Minnesota career on a poor note with a bad interception on his first passing attempt of Sunday's game. But later in the first quarter, Murray took a big hit from two Packers defenders that ended with his helmet flying off his head.

Murray stayed down for a while before walking off the field and into the locker room. Javon Bullard , whose forceful blow knocked off Murray's helmet, was flagged for a personal foul (unnecessary roughness).

On Monday, O'Connell said that there was no one to blame for the hit on Murray.

"It would be one thing if there was a headfirst slide and a clear declaration [of giving himself up]," O'Connell said, via ESPN . "But I don't put any fault on anybody there."

In addition to Murray being out, the Vikings also announced that wide receiver Jauan Jennings would be out due to a non-injury reason. O'Connell told reporters on Friday that Jennings was dealing with a "personal family matter."

articles.title: Joe Burrow, Nico Collins, NFL Injury Statuses and Fantasy Impact for Week 2
articles.summary: Two of the most impactful fantasy football point earners in the AFC are under the injury microscope ahead of Week 2.
articles.body:
Two of the most impactful fantasy football point earners in the AFC are under the injury microscope ahead of Week 2.

Joe Burrow has been dealing with a back issue this week, but all signs point to him being on the field on Sunday for the Cincinnati Bengals.

Nico Collins is not as fortunate, as it looks like he'll sit out Week 2 for the Houston Texans with a hamstring injury.

Below is a look at all of the notable fantasy football injury news ahead of Week 2's games.

Joe Burrow's back tightness will not keep him out of the Week 2 clash with the Texans despite officially being listed as questionable.

ESPN's Adam Schefter reported earlier this week that the issue is not serious enough to rule him out for the trip to Texas.

WLWT's Charlie Clifford noted on Friday that Burrow didn't have many limitations in the throws he made.

Burrow threw for 254 yards and a touchdown in Week 1. That is close to the expected stat line each week for the Cincinnati quarterback, especially with Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins at his disposal.

Burrow and the Bengals do have a tougher matchup on paper in Week 2 against one of the best defenses in the NFL.

Houston allowed Josh Allen to throw for 334 yards in Week 1, so there is hope that the Bengals stars put up large fantasy football totals.

It's understandable if you'd like to start someone else at quarterback based on matchup , but there's no reason to leave Burrow out of your lineup due to his health.

KPRC's Aaron Wilson noted that Collins didn't participate in Friday's practice. He has since been ruled out.

Collins hauled in seven receptions on 10 targets for 75 yards and a touchdown in Week 1 against the Bills.

He's obviously going to be a massive loss for the Texans in their AFC showdown with the Bengals.

Jaylin Noel, Xavier Hutchinson and Kayshon Boutte are the wide receivers to look at from a fantasy perspective, but the biggest beneficiary might be tight end Dalton Schultz.

Schultz had the second-most targets on the Texans roster behind Collins in Week 1. He's the most reliable pass-catcher at C.J. Stroud's disposal for Week 2.

Chicago's Luther Burden III and Minnesota's Jordan Addison are among the ideal replacements for Collins should you have them at your disposal. The Bears play the Vikings in Week 2 in a matchup of two teams that gave up over 300 passing yards in Week 1.

Kansas City's Xavier Worthy and Quentin Johnston of the Los Angeles Chargers are other players to target because of their respective Week 2 matchups.

Unfortunately for fantasy players, there will be a drop off in production of some sort from Collins to whomever replaces him because he is one of the highest-volume pass-catchers in the NFL.

articles.title: Patriots coach Mike Vrabel does about-face on TreVeyon Henderson's activism after Russini scandal
articles.summary: Mike Vrabel's tone on TreVeyon Henderson's social issues advocacy shifted dramatically since April, when the Patriots coach had urged caution.
articles.body: New England Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel has softened his stance on running back TreVeyon Henderson’s social activism since April, when he cautioned the player to remember that he represents the team. Vrabel was asked Friday about Henderson’s defense of a Massachusetts couple who say they lost custody of their daughter to DCF after refusing to allow her to transition to a boy. Authorities have made it clear that the issue had to do with allegations of abuse by the couple, although they have not been convicted of any crime. TREVEYON HENDERSON EXPLAINS SIDING WITH FAMILY OVER DCF IN CUSTODY DISPUTE INVOLVING GENDER IDENTITY Henderson spent significant time the past couple of days defending the couple on social media and with beat reporters on Thursday. And, none of this has really anything to do with football. But Vrabel was asked on Friday how he views Henderson's public position considering in April the coach spoke about there being a "fine line" when it comes to expressing personal beliefs publicly. "I think he's handled it, I mean, about as maturely," Vrabel said. "I think he tried to explain himself. TreVeyon is a special person, great teammate. I love being around him. "And I think he pretty much spoke on what he thought and what he believes, and I think that that's impressive. You know, for him to be able to speak on it, and [I] leave it up to him." So, who is this coach? He is very different from the one who sat at a roundtable with reporters during the NFL annual meeting in Arizona in April and did not embrace Henderson advocating on behalf of former Chicago Bulls player Jaden Ivey. Ivey, you may recall, was released by the Bulls after he spoke out against the NBA promoting Pride Month and "unrighteousness." THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! This is how Vrabel reacted to Henderson's defense of Ivey in April. "I think there's a fine line," Vrabel said. "I'll tell you, I love TreVeyon. I love the person. He cares deeply about our team. He cares deeply about his faith. He cares deeply about his family. His wife. The people in our building. "And so, I want them to be able to express what they believe in their heart and in their mind. But also, I want to make sure that they're educated. We want to be inclusive. Everything we want to do wants to provide an environment for people to feel comfortable. "But also to share their personal beliefs and, also, we represent the team and we represent the organization." There was none of that get "educated" talk from Vrabel on Friday because perhaps he realized those comments suggested his player didn't know what he was talking about. And there was definitely none of the "represent the team" narrative from Vrabel because, well, we know why. Vrabel didn't exactly "represent" the Patriots well during the offseason when it was discovered by Page Six that he spent the days prior to an Arizona meeting with former NFL reporter Dianna Russini at a Sedona resort. It wasn’t a good look for the Patriots that their married coach was photographed with a married female reporter holding hands, embracing and spending time together at a pool and hot tub. That entire episode was obviously embarrassing for Vrabel. But perhaps it was also instructive in that he has realized a player taking a moral stand on a topic is not representing the team poorly regardless of whether some people disagree or not. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP So, maybe something good has come out of the Russini scandal for Vrabel. Maybe. FOLLOW ARMANDO SALGUERO ON X: @ARMANDOSALGUERO

articles.summary: Las Vegas Raiders (1-0) AT LA Chargers (0-1)When: Sunday 1:05 pmWhere: SoFi StadiumTV: CBS-2 (Los Angeles), CBS-8 (San Diego), Paramount/NFL+ Radio: Los Ange...
articles.body:
Las Vegas Raiders (1-0) AT LA Chargers (0-1)

TV: CBS-2 ( Los Angeles ), CBS-8 (San Diego), Paramount/NFL+

Radio: Los Angeles: KYSR-FM (98.7), LA Spanish: Latino Mix 103.9/89.3 FM

articles.title: Sam Darnold Injury Update Given By Mike Macdonald Ahead of NFL Week 2 Amid Glute Issue
articles.summary: Seattle Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald provided a new update regarding the health of quarterback Sam Darnold on Friday.
articles.body:
Seattle Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald provided a new update regarding the health of quarterback Sam Darnold on Friday.

"He's on his way back," Macdonald said, via Josh Alper of Pro Football Talk. "Is it next week? Is it the week after, the week after that? I'm not sure. I'm optimistic, put it that way."

Darnold was previously ruled out of the Seahawks' Week 2 matchup with the Arizona Cardinals due to a glute injury that he suffered in the first quarter of their season-opening win over the New England Patriots.

He didn't participate in practice throughout the week leading up to Sunday's clash with Arizona.

The Seahawks described his health issue as a "very unique soft-tissue" injury that isn't expected to sideline him long term, per ESPN's Brady Henderson . Seattle also chose not to place Darnold on injured reserve, which indicates that the team believes he can back within its next four games.

The 29-year-old wrapped up a 2025 campaign in which he started all 17 regular-season games before helping the Seahawks capture their second Super Bowl title.

Darnold threw for 4,048 yards and 25 touchdowns compared to 14 interceptions last season, compiling a career-high 67.7 completion percentage. He earned a Pro Bowl nod for his efforts.

Until Darnold is able to return, the Seahawks will continue to rely on Drew Lock as their starter under center. Second-year passer Jalen Milroe is also available as a reserve option.

Lock replaced Darnold in Week 1, finishing 16-of-22 for 187 yards and one touchdown without getting picked off. He helped the Seahawks come back from a 10-point deficit in the second half to secure a 13-10 win over New England.

Darnold's next opportunity to play will come during Seattle's Week 3 game against the Washington Commanders on Sept. 27.

articles.title: Aaron Donald Gives Status Update for Rams vs. Giants Amid Rumors After Comeback From Retirement
articles.summary: Even though the Los Angeles Rams won't have Myles Garrett for a while due to a knee injury, they are likely going to have Aaron Donald in Week 2 against the New York Giants.
articles.body:
Even though the Los Angeles Rams won't have Myles Garrett for a while due to a knee injury, they are likely going to have Aaron Donald in Week 2 against the New York Giants.

Speaking to reporters after Friday's practice, Donald said "that's the plan" when asked if he would be playing on Monday Night Football against the Giants.

Donald did not travel to Australia with the Rams for their Week 1 matchup against the San Francisco 49ers. The reasoning was they wanted to give him a longer ramp-up period as he returns to the NFL two years after his initial retirement.

After Donald took part in multiple workouts with the Rams during training camp, he officially rejoined the team on Aug. 30 by signing a one-year deal that could max out at $30 million.

Week 1 turned into a disaster for the Rams with a 27-7 loss to the 49ers. It marked their lowest point total in 75 games started by Matthew Stafford.

Adding injury to insult, four days after the loss, it was reported Garrett will be placed on injured reserve due to a knee injury that requires arthroscopic knee surgery. An IR stint requires him to miss at least four games, meaning Week 6 against the Arizona Cardinals is the earliest he can return.

Now that Donald has confirmed he plans to play in Week 2, the next question is how frequently he will be on the field. It has been suggested he could play around 30-40 snaps per game, though it's unclear if that's what he will average over the full season or if he will start at that threshold and maintain it.

The Rams can certainly use any boost that Donald can provide going into a matchup with the Giants that looks more competitive now than when the schedule was first released in May.

New York is coming off an impressive 28-20 win over the Dallas Cowboys in Week 1. The Giants put up 394 yards of offense, including 165 rushing yards, and held the ball for nearly 37 minutes.

A loss would drop the Rams, who were strong favorites to win the Super Bowl coming into the season, to 0-2 with their next three games against the Denver Broncos, Philadelphia Eagles and Buffalo Bills.

Assuming Donald does play, it will be his first appearance in an NFL game sinceJan. 14, 2024. He made the All-Pro first team in nine of his first 10 seasons and won three Defensive Player of the Year awards.

articles.title: Aaron Donald says he plans to make 2026 debut in Rams' MNF game vs. Giants
articles.summary: Donald's last NFL game was on Jan. 14, 2024.
articles.body:
It looks like Aaron Donald 's two-year retirement is officially ending on Monday.

The three-time Defensive Player of the Year told reporters on Friday that he intends to play in the Los Angeles Rams ' "Monday Night Football" game against the New York Giants in Week 2, via the team :

"That's the plan. Two practices today, have another practice tomorrow and then we'll see, but feeling good."

The last game Donald played was the Rams' wild-card round loss to the Detroit Lions on Jan. 14, 2024. He appeared happy in what turned out to be his first retirement, but rumblings of a return came soon after the Rams' blockbuster trade for star pass-rusher Myles Garrett .

Donald slowly deliberated over a return, with the Rams providing sporadic updates as he went through the motions of figuring out whether he was ready to play in the NFL again. The answer finally came on Aug. 30, with Donald signing a one-year, $20 million deal to play for the Rams again .

That return came too late for Donald to play in the Rams' season-opener against the San Francisco 49ers in Australia, a 27-7 blowout loss . That also represented Donald's first chance to play alongside Garrett, who was invisible in Week 1 then underwent knee surgery.

Garrett is now on injured reserve and will be out for at least four weeks. Via The Athletic's Nate Atkins , Donald hopes to keep things together until he comes back:

"I think we've got a great defense, a great team, a lot of great pieces. Obviously, I would love for him to be out there, but he won't be gone forever. ... Hold it down while he's gone."

Even with an extended layoff, expectations will be high for Donald, just as they've been for the entire Rams team that entered this season as the Super Bowl favorite. At 35 years old, Donald might occupy a different role than the one he had in his prime, but we know one thing for sure: it will be worth watching.

The Rams are scheduled to kick off against the Giants at 5:15 p.m. PT on Monday.

articles.title: Broncos focused on slowing down Jaguars potent offense
articles.summary: Trevor Lawrence and the Jacksonville Jaguars offense will be a tough test for the Denver Broncos on Sunday.
articles.body:
The Denver Broncos host the Jacksonville Jaguars on Sunday for their Week 2 matchup. Coming off a tough loss to the Kansas City Chiefs , the Broncos are trying to rectify what all went wrong and be at their best to go up against a well-coached Jacksonville team.

Last season, the Broncos had one of the best defenses in the National Football League. Few teams gave them major issues, but the Jaguars were one of them. Led by Trevor Lawrence , their offense scored 34 points against the Broncos—the most of any opponent. They had 346 yards of total offense and amassed a whopping 22 first downs. But where they really excelled was on third down, completing over 50-percent of their attempts.

Today after practice, Head Coach Sean Payton had high praise for Lawrence and how formidable their offense has become under Liam Coen.

"They're doing a great job. He's got a big arm. All of the things we saw when he came out as a high draft pick. These big quarterbacks who can move and he's one of them, to the right, to the left. If you get caught in a man defense and you're not rushing properly, he can pick up eight yards on a third-and-four easily. Then just the surrounding cast, you can tell they've been together. They're confident in what they're doing," stated Payton.

Under Coen's leadership, Jacksonville jumped from 26th in points scored in 2024 to being sixth in the NFL in 2025. They went from a four-win team in '24 to one that won thirteen games just a season ago. Their transformation on offense played a big part in that. This season, they started off strong with an impressive victory over the Cleveland Browns where Lawrence was able to score four touchdowns.

Denver has to find a way to limit Lawrence's impact on the game. Though he isn't the only player they have to take notice of. The Jaguars have a talented core of skill positions players that all offer unique skill sets. Defensive Coordinator Vance Joseph offered his thoughts on their offense and who they will need to slow down in order to achieve a victory.

"I thought Trevor from mid-season last year to now; he's playing like a Top 5 guy. He has a bunch of weapons. The runner Bhayshul Tuten is very explosive. He's a 4.3 guy, but he runs hard. He has this compact body, so again the tackle surface is very minimal. You need hats to the ball. Your eyes have to be right when you're tackling backs like that," stated Joseph.

A fourth-round pick by the Jaguars in the 2025 NFL Draft, Tuten earned the starting role this offseason after Travis Etienne 's departure to the New Orleans Saints . Appearing in fifteen games as a rookie, Tuten notched 386 all-purpose yards and 7 touchdowns. In the season opener against Cleveland, he had 16 total touches for 88 yards and five first downs. He also forced seven missed tackles—something the Broncos can't afford to let happen again this week.

In addition to Tuten, Joseph mentioned several of their wide receivers who stood out to him last year and while watching film.

"Parker Washington came on really late last year against us and kind of moved forward to be a real guy as a punt returner and as a receiver. He's playing well. Jakobi Meyers is playing well as a blocker, a receiver, screen game, all those things he's doing well. It's going to be a challenge schematically, and to win some one-on-ones and to obviously tackle better."

Washington had six receptions for 145 yards and a touchdown against the Broncos last December . It was one of the best games of his career. In turn, it was one of the worst for nickelback Ja'Quan McMillian who struggled to combat Washington's speed and ability at the line of scrimmage. Finding a way to limit Washington's big play ability is essential for the Broncos on Sunday.

Make no mistake, Broncos Country—the Jaguars are a very good team. Denver will have to be at their best to forego starting their '26 gridiron campaign 0-2.

articles.title: Quarterback guru explains why Bear Bachmeier’s deep ball works (+predictions)
articles.summary: Former BYU and NFL QB John Beck spent time with Cougars quarterback during the summer. Here’s what they worked on — and why.
articles.body:
It's a footnote of sorts, but it makes a huge difference in BYU's offense heading into its third game of the season at Colorado State.

It is Bear Bachmeier's added skill to go deep . And somebody who can get deep.

The Cougars are favored to beat CSU in Fort Collins and Utah is expected to run over Utah State at home on Saturday.

The 11th-ranked Cougars feature Big 12 Offensive Player of the Year LJ Martain as a run threat. The offense fields a very tall receiving corps alongside a talented tight end group. The addition of sensational freshman Legend Glasker , who can take the top off a defense by going deep, is a big deal for offensive coordinator Aaron Roderick.

This was the case in BYU's second-half surge against Arizona last week when Bachmeier used a play-action fake to set up a drop-back throw to Glasker for 61 yards and, well, all but seal the win in the fourth quarter.

What did Bachmeier do in the offseason to add this to his arsenal? Why is he able to throw from the 20 to the 20, making Glasker a weapon that must be either double covered with a corner and safety, or at least make defenses account for that ability?

Well, it took some work and some focus during the summer.

Bachmeier, like Arizona's Noah Fifita and many of the top college and NFL quarterbacks around the country, has worked with 3DQB in Southern California. One of the instructors, former BYU quarterback John Beck , explained exactly what that entailed for Bachmeier entering his sophomore season.

"I would just say he recognized it was an area that he wanted to be able to improve on, and that was just driving the ball downfield. And so, it's not a capacity thing," said Beck in a Thursday telephone chat with the Deseret News. "It is being able to kind of harness what's there and really get it in sequence. He's a very powerful kid, you know. That's easy to see.

"He wanted to be able to drive the ball down the field easier and not have some of his balls downfield kind of hang on him and float, so that was a bit of an emphasis in some of our training things."

Beck said on that 61-yard throw to Glasker, Bachmeier didn't have to take a big move, like climbing the pocket with a big hitching movement. "He just was able to set his feet and send a ball down that field that he was really happy about."

What Bachmeier has done doesn't have anything to do with his athleticism or capacity as a quarterback, but more to do with positioning with his launch.

Beck explained that quarterbacks these days have spent most of their careers throwing passes behind, at or 15 to 20 yards beyond the line of scrimmage. That's where their plays are designed.

So QBs get used to throwing those passes using their skill and athleticism and in their minds, they can do that, throw off different platforms, throw on the move or sprinting out and hitting targets at different angles.

But to throw deep takes a different position and mindset, breaking the mold of what they are used to doing with a pass play.

"Bear is a very twitchy individual, and he can get the ball out really fast, and he can change arm angles. He has all those things.

"And sometimes what happens is you build so much of your pattern based off of the throws that you make the majority of the time. And so for today's offenses, there're a lot of balls that are at the line of scrimmage, barely beyond the line of scrimmage. You know, you play a lot of your game within 15 to 20 yards and in. So what can happen sometimes is a quarterback just builds his positions and his sequence in something like, 'Oh, I can make that throw really quick.'

"They can build a body position where, because their upper body alone can just get the ball out there, it works. So for Bear, it was more of getting him to feel the right position and the right timing to be able to utilize his full capacity in delivering those balls downfield."

Beck said Bachmeier has a baseball background, and he can sometimes put himself in a body position that is not necessarily the best, but he can make the throw because of everything else around him by just sheer arm talent and twitchiness.

"Bear can do that. He doesn't always have to be in the best platform to make a lot of the throws that he makes, and he gets the ball out very quickly when he does that.

"But the tough part is, when your body starts to learn that pattern and it starts to utilize that pattern the majority of the time, then when you go to find the position that you need to deliver a ball downfield, that's less familiar, right? And so you're utilizing a position and a platform that is built for the short to intermediate throws when trying to deliver a downfield throw."

In BYU's first two games, Bachmeier is 32 of 46, completing 69.6% of his passes for a 9.0 average per completion with six touchdowns, zero interceptions and 188 pass efficiency.

articles.title: FBI identifies 35 additional women who claim they were defrauded by alleged scheme that featured fake 49ers player
articles.summary: There are now 61 potential victims in the case.
articles.body:
The U.S. Attorney's office in the District of Oregon announced last month that a man masquerading as a San Francisco 49ers player was part of a wire fraud scheme that exploited 26 then-known victims of more than $1.3 million across California, Idaho, Washington and Oregon.

FBI special agent Douglas A. Olson revealed Friday that federal investigators have identified 35 additional women who claim they were defrauded by 35-year-old Daejon Love and 18-year-old Taylor Chan, according to multiple reports .

Olson said the agency is in the process of verifying that the 35 women are victims of Love and Chan, per ESPN .

There are now 61 potential victims in the case.

Love and Chan were arrested on Aug. 24. The duo has been charged with conspiracy to commit wire fraud and wire fraud. They were apprehended at the Boise Airport in Idaho, where Love was set to meet new victims, per investigators .

During a news conference on Friday, Olson emphasized that anyone could have been a victim of the alleged fraud, as reported by The Oregonian/OregonLive .

"Victim blaming is unjust, and it's harmful, and it overlooks the calculated, highly-manipulated lengths these individuals went to in order to deceive and exploit others," Olson reportedly said.

"The women didn't just fall for something obvious; they were deliberately targeted by people who worked very hard to earn that trust and steal their money."

Love, who the U.S. Attorney's office says repeatedly posed as a Niners player or as a wealthy real estate investor, is still in custody in Boise, per The Oregonian/OregonLive, which reported that he's expected to make a federal court appearance next month in Portland.

Chan, who the U.S. Attorney's office says acted as Love's financial adviser, reportedly already appeared in federal court in Portland this month. He was released pending trial, according to The Oregonian/OregonLive.

The alleged scheme spanned four years, beginning in February 2022. Love and Chan targeted women in the four aforementioned states out west, most of whom Love met through dating apps, prosecutors said. Along with his actual name, Love used several other names — including Jon Love, Avril Lyto Love and Jordan Love — while carrying out the caper, per the U.S. Attorney's office.

"Love convinced many of the victims they were in sincere romantic relationships with Love, that he was a sophisticated investor, and that Chan was his investment adviser who helped Love grow a fortune worth tens of millions of dollars," the U.S. Attorney's Office Aug. 25 statement said. "Love had romantic relationships with many of the victims and told them he wanted to build wealth and a future together. Love advertised nonexistent investment vehicles and claimed these investments would generate massive returns for both him and his victims."

Phony bank and investment accounts and balances, created via phone applications, allegedly allowed Love to strengthen the validity of the ploy. Chan and Love even held three-way FaceTimes to flaunt falsified investment gains to whichever victim was on the call, according to the U.S. Attorney's office.

Love also attempted to bolster his fake identities with AI-enhanced images, according to Olson, The Oregonian/OregonLive reported.

Victims sent Love and Chan money with the intent that it would be deployed for fruitful investments overseen by the tandem, prosecutors said.

"Once victims had no more money to invest, or if they asked too many questions, Love blocked communication with them but kept their money," the U.S. Attorney's office Aug. 25 statement said.

At the time of that statement, of the victims who had been identified and interviewed upon sending Love and Chan money, "none reported receiving any proceeds, returns on their principle, or investment account information," according to prosecutors.

Olson said Friday that the FBI believes there are even more victims out there and that the agency encourages them to come forward, per ESPN's report.

As for the 49ers organization, "they were completely cooperative," Olson reportedly said. "They were very helpful in doing things that most people think are probably pretty simple, but it's not always that easy to confirm," he said, according to ESPN. "Like, this person was never an employee, never a player, not even ever in the NFL. They were able to help with a lot of that stuff."
